articles.title_orig: A busted-down door, an FBI search and a one-way ticket to China: Feds ask if accused Chinese agent had help
articles.title_zh: A busted-down door, an FBI search and a one-way ticket to China: Feds ask if accused Chinese agent had help
articles.content_orig:
The alleged Chinese agent arrested at Los Angeles International Airport on Sunday may have had help, according to the FBI.
Fatai Miao, a Chinese-born California construction entrepreneur, is the man believed to have accompanied realtor Wanying Zhang to Seattle in September 2025, where she allegedly surveilled the Taiwanese president's son, CBS News has learned.
Through federal documents, law enforcement sources and interviews with his family and neighbors, CBS News confirmed Miao's identity.
Miao took a "one-way" flight to China two weeks ago, prosecutors said in court on Wednesday, referring to him as "Individual 1." The Justice Department has not accused him of any wrongdoing, and a relative described him as a "follower" who would not participate in any sophisticated government activity.
Miao's neighbors in Irvine, California, said about 10 FBI agents serving a search warrant broke into his empty home using a battering ram around noon on Sunday, shortly after Zhang was arrested trying to board a flight to Shanghai.
Miao's U.S.-resident son, contacted by phone on Tuesday evening, said his father has been in China for the last two weeks to look after his wife, who recently traveled there to receive medical care for her back.
Miao allegedly joined Zhang in Seattle on Sept. 1, 2025, rented an SUV, and was in the car while she allegedly filmed Taiwan's first son returning to his suburban home with his wife and child, according to documents filed in federal court, which identified him only as "Individual 1."
Prosecutors claim Zhang was conducting the surveillance on the orders of Chinese government officials, after meeting with them in China to plan the mission the previous month.
The FBI agent who wrote an affidavit for the criminal complaint against Zhang left a trail of clues that helped CBS News reveal Miao as the likely unnamed travel companion.
Counterintelligence Squad Special Agent Kevin Holt wrote that the paperwork for the car that Zhang and "Individual 1" rented on their alleged Seattle surveillance trip listed the address of a home on Walnut Avenue in Arcadia, California, that he owned at the time.
"Based on public records, I know that Individual 1 sold a house at this address on or about September 11, 2025," the FBI agent wrote.
Property records show the only house on that street sold on that date belonged to Miao.
CBS News has learned that Miao is a person of interest in the FBI's Zhang investigation.
Miao's current home, in a newly built housing complex in Irvine, has remained empty since the FBI raided it on Sunday, neighbors said.
When a CBS News reporter visited the property on Tuesday, the handle on the front door was snapped and there was a large dent that splintered the wood beside it. The home's video doorbell had been ripped from the wall.
The only sign of life at the house was three pairs of flip-flops left on the front patio.
"Me and my sister got a call on Sunday noon," said Miao's son, Jiaqi Miao, in a telephone interview. "Someone says he's from the FBI and he has a search warrant. I thought he's a scammer.
"Then I checked the security camera at our house and I see several government agents holding a gun outside. I was trying to open the door for them using the remote app, but it was too late. They already used the door breach thing," he added.
Jiaqi Miao said the agents arrived in "five or six SUVs and one big truck."
Neighbors' accounts of the raid matched Jiaqi Miao's description.
He said his father had been friends with Zhang for over a decade, after she showed him a condo he was considering buying. He said she lived temporarily at Fatai Miao's Arcadia property about 10 years ago.
"We rented her the pool house for a few months," he said. "I think her own house had some renovations going on."
A neighbor, who declined to give his full name, said he was friendly with the elder Miao, and that he had recently attended a dinner party with several guests including Fatai Miao and Zhang.
Jiaqi Miao said although the FBI's description of "Individual 1" in the complaint "sounds like him," he said he does not believe his father, who he says does not speak English, is an unregistered agent for the Chinese government.
"To be honest, I don't think he's smart enough to do those things," Jiaqi Miao said. "He always follows others. For example, he doesn't understand soccer, but he went to the World Cup because his friend told him it's a big event."
The elder Miao is CEO of several companies, according to California corporation records, including Jiacheng Real Estate Investment and Management Inc., Jin Yuan Investment LLC, M & Y Construction LLC, and NeoBio USA LLC.
The company J&J California Construction, registered at Fatai Miao's Walnut Avenue address, held a general contractor license that expired last year.
"The reason he came to the U.S. is because my parents think me and my sister can get better education here," Jiaqi said. "My father is the only one in our family to choose to get U.S. citizenship. That's why I think there's no reason why he would want to work with the Chinese government."
Jiaqi Miao said he suspects that his father's trip to Seattle with Zhang occurred innocently after hearing his friend wanted to visit a different city.
Jiaqi said he spoke with his father on the phone from China after the raid. He said his father told him he learned of Zhang's arrest from a friend, and reassured his son that "everything is fine."
The son, who attends school in the U.S., said Fatai Miao is now looking to hire a lawyer.
A judge denied Zhang's attorney's request to release her on bail during a hearing on Wednesday .
Prosecutors told the court she poses a serious flight risk, in part due to her access to "hundreds of thousands of dollars" in China.
Assistant U.S. Attorney Amanda Elbogen said Zhang had deposited $170,000 in a Chinese bank account from an "unregistered cryptocurrency exchange business," that she had a Chinese passport that law enforcement had been unable to find, and that her parents and siblings live in China — including a brother who she claimed worked for the Chinese government.
CBS News previously revealed Zhang's links to a Chinese American advocacy group with deep ties to the Chinese government.
She traveled to San Francisco with the organization, the All American Chinese Association, to celebrate Chinese President Xi Jinping's visit there in 2023.
Pro-China activists then attacked pro-democracy protesters outside Xi's hotel, though there is no evidence Zhang was involved in the violence.
A photograph shows her behind an AACA banner, standing next to the group's leader, Edward Cai, who previously served as vice president for an organization so close to the Chinese government it was forced to register under the Foreign Agents Registration Act (FARA).
FARA requires agents of foreign governments to inform the Justice Department of their status and any lobbying, attempted influence, or other activities in the U.S.

articles.title_orig: Ithaca council passes moratorium on new Cornell events permits, calls for city police to handle sexual violence cases
articles.title_zh: Ithaca council passes moratorium on new Cornell events permits, calls for city police to handle sexual violence cases
articles.content_orig:
The Ithaca Common Council voted Wednesday night to pass a temporary moratorium on special events permits at Cornell University and called on the school to hand over investigations into "violent sex crimes" to the Ithaca Police Department.
The moratorium will apply to Cornell University, its residential and nonresidential sorority and fraternity organizations, general student organizations, and university student affiliations, according to Ithaca's mayor, Robert Cantelmo.
Effective immediately, the city will not issue new permits to the affected parties for assemblies, parades, special events and noise. The moratorium, which is set to expire on Nov. 5, passed by a 9-1 vote and is designed so that the council can choose to renew it on a monthly basis.
Cantelmo said the council adopted the moratorium "based on substantial concerns for the safety, health, and welfare of the residents of, and visitors to, the city of Ithaca."
The council also amended the moratorium Wednesday night to include a resolution "that the city calls upon Cornell to hand over investigation of violent sex crimes" to the Ithaca Police Department.
Cantelmo said the city is demanding the school do more to "punish, monitor transparently and prevent sexual violence on campus."
The mayor proposed the moratorium on campus events in the wake of a civil lawsuit filed last month by a former Cornell student, Jane Doe , who alleged she was drugged and gang-raped by seven fraternity brothers at the Chi Phi house in October 2024.
She reported the alleged assault to the Cornell University Police Department three weeks later. The department turned over a summary of her allegations in a sworn statement to the district attorney, who decided not to pursue charges. Ithaca Police say they were not informed of the case.
In response to an investigation by Cornell's Title IX office, the school said that two of the men were expelled, two were suspended for at least two semesters, one had already graduated before any punishment could be handed down, and two were found not to be responsible for sexual misconduct.
After the woman filed her lawsuit and details of the allegations became public, New York Gov. Kathy Hochul appointed state Attorney General Letitia James as special prosecutor to review the case.
On Cornell's campus, students have held rallies and protests to express anger with the school administration's handling of the allegations, and to stand in solidarity with sexual violence survivors. On Monday, over 1,000 people, including students, professors and local Ithaca residents, gathered to demand change from the school. On Wednesday, more than 100 students staged a seven-hour sit-in at a dining hall.
A 2025 survey conducted by Cornell found that more than one in three undergraduate women reported nonconsensual sexual contact involving force or incapacitation since entering the school. More than 49% of respondents reported harassment. The survey identified campus-affiliated settings like residence halls and fraternity houses as the location of most incidents.
Cecily Cox, a graduate student at Cornell who opposes the moratorium, addressed the council Wednesday night at the meeting where it passed.
"Parties do not cause sexual violence," Cox told CBS News.
She took issue with the moratorium's "ambiguity" and said it will affect more students than necessary.
It "should not be for all students and should not punish all students who have nothing to do with what is going on with the sexual assault case," Cox said.
Cantelmo said the moratorium is not intended to be applied in a way that would infringe on any student's right to exercise freedom of religion, speech or peaceful assembly.
Social events that would not otherwise have needed a permit will not be affected, according to a city official. Permits relating to free speech or assembly events will not be denied because of this moratorium, the official said. Through the moratorium, Ithaca is hoping to start a process of the city and school working more closely together to create a safe and healthy environment for students.
Some students, like Sam Poole, believe the moratorium is an opportunity for the city to put pressure on the school.
"Cornell's already feeling this pressure, and we need the city to keep this moratorium in place until they actually make structural change," said Poole.
"Cornell will not protect survivors unless somebody forces them to," Poole added. "I think the city of Ithaca has the power by threatening the thing they care about, which is their events."

articles.title_orig: Venezuela's Maduro, wife Flores tortured opponents to stay in power, US prosecutors say
articles.title_zh: Venezuela's Maduro, wife Flores tortured opponents to stay in power, US prosecutors say
articles.content_orig:
NEW YORK — Former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro has been charged by U.S. authorities with torture and other crimes in a new indictment unsealed Thursday that adds pressure on the ousted authoritarian leader already fighting drug trafficking offenses.
Maduro, who was previously charged with participating in a conspiracy to send cocaine into the U.S., is now also facing allegations of human rights abuses during his reign as president of the oil-rich South American nation.
Maduro and his wife, Cilia Flores, have been behind bars in New York since early January when forces seized them from their Caracas home in a middle-of-the-night raid.
Both have pleaded not guilty in the criminal case first brought years ago against them and numerous alleged co-conspirators. They had already been facing potential life prison sentences if convicted.
Cilia Flores was scheduled to be in court Thursday, where her lawyers will urge a judge to free her from jail and put her under house arrest because she has heart problems.
Their attorneys have asked for the case to be dismissed on the grounds that they have immunity as the leader and first lady of a foreign country.
Lawyers for Flores, 69, have also argued that she has medical issues that cannot be treated effectively in jail, and that she could instead be allowed to live under 24-hour guard at a residence in New York.
They also said she suffered permanent scarring when she was “thrown against a wall or dresser” during the U.S. military action that led to her capture.
Her lawyers say she has lost 25 pounds (11 kilograms) while imprisoned at the Metropolitan Detention Center in Brooklyn and has been told that she might need heart surgery. They said she has “lingering lightheadedness, dizziness and shortness of breath” and might have suffered a minor heart attack in July.
Prosecutors opposed the bail request. In a court filing, they wrote that Flores would pose an “extreme risk of flight and danger to the public” if released. They also said she has been taken from the jail to get treatment at a local hospital, when care was needed.
President Donald Trump’s administration has defended the raid to capture Maduro as a “surgical law enforcement operation.” Maduro has called himself a prisoner of war and his capture a kidnapping.
Flores is charged with participating in a cocaine importation conspiracy with her husband, Maduro, who served as Venezuela’s president from 2013 until his capture by American forces in January.
Lawyers for Flores said she was no threat to flee because she is “intent on supporting her husband with her constant presence.”

articles.title_orig: Sony Electronics Announces the World's First Eclipsa Audio Certified Spatial Audio Microphone for Smartphones¹
articles.title_zh: Sony Electronics Announces the World's First Eclipsa Audio Certified Spatial Audio Microphone for Smartphones¹
articles.content_orig:
ECM-AX10 is a portable USB-C spatial audio microphone designed to help vloggers, mobile filmmakers, and content creators capture spatial sound, edit on the go, and export videos with spatial audio
SAN DIEGO , Oct. 8, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Sony Electronics Inc. today announced the ECM-AX10, the world's first Eclipsa Audio 2 -certified microphone for smartphones. Created for vloggers, mobile filmmakers, and content creators, the ECM-AX10 helps capture sound that feels more natural, immersive, and true to the moment. Its four built-in omnidirectional microphone capsules record sound from multiple directions, while Sony's spatial audio processing recreates a sense of space, direction, and distance that can make videos feel more engaging and immersive for viewers.
Small and lightweight, the microphone connects directly to compatible smartphones 3 via USB-C ® 4 and gives creators three easy ways to capture sound: Ambisonics recording for spatial audio production, binaural recording for an immersive headphone experience, and stereo recording for everyday videos and social content.
When used with Sony's dedicated Spatial Audio Video Tool 5 app, creators can shoot video, check footage, make simple edits, and export content with spatial audio 6 . This allows users to complete the entire production workflow for spatial audio video on their smartphone.
Spatial audio for smartphone video The ECM-AX10 is designed to make smartphone videos sound bigger, natural, and true to the moment. Sony's newly developed spherical microphone module uses four omnidirectional microphone capsules to support Ambisonics recording, helping capture sound from all directions. With advanced spatial audio processing, creators can bring through the atmosphere, direction, and distance of a place, from street performances and festivals to sports, travel content, and behind-the-scenes moments, so viewers feel closer to the action.
Three recording modes for different creator approaches Creators can choose from three recording modes to suit their content, platform, and playback needs:
Compact USB-C design for filming on the move Weighing approximately 24g, the ECM-AX10 is designed to be carried anywhere and set up quickly for spontaneous filming. The direct USB-C ® connection helps creators capture higher-quality audio without a separate recorder or complex setup, supporting a simple smartphone-first production workflow. With the Spatial Audio Video Tool app 5 , users can record video 8 , review clips, make quick edits, and export finished content with spatial audio entirely on their smartphone, streamlining the journey from capture to share.
Developed with sound engineers To help ensure the ECM-AX10 delivers an authentic and immersive listening experience, Sony Electronics worked with Sony PCL, a Sony Group company with extensive expertise in planning and producing content and spatial experiences. Leveraging the knowledge it has developed through post-production, where video and audio are refined into their final form, Sony PCL supported the sound quality tuning of the microphone.
Sony PCL Sound Engineer Mr. Iwana commented: "The orchestral sound recorded with the ECM-AX10 captures the music with remarkable depth, with quick response in the low and low-mid ranges, while the high frequencies are expansive and moving. For ambient sound, it also delivers an impressive sense of presence, richly reproducing the three-dimensionality of sound and the spaciousness of a 360-degree sound field. I believe this microphone can vividly capture even the atmosphere of the moment, together with a three-dimensional sense of realism, elevating important videos into works that feel more real and memorable."
Pricing and availability The ECM-AX10 is available for pre-sale now for MSRP $249.99 USD/ $349.99 CAN priced at Sony , Amazon , B&H, Best Buy, Sweetwater. Guitar Center, and other authorized dealers.
For more information about Sony's ECM-AX10 compact spatial audio microphone for smartphones, visit https://electronics.sony.com/audio/professional-audio/all-professional-audio/p/ecmax10b .
About Sony Electronics, Inc.
Sony Electronics is a subsidiary of Sony Corporation of America and an affiliate of Sony Group Corporation, one of the most comprehensive entertainment companies in the world, with a portfolio that encompasses electronics, music, motion pictures, mobile, gaming, robotics and financial services. Headquartered in San Diego, California, Sony Electronics is a leader in electronics for the consumer and professional markets. Operations include research and development, engineering, sales, marketing, distribution and customer service. Sony Electronics creates products that innovate and inspire generations, such as the award-winning Alpha Interchangeable Lens Cameras and revolutionary high-resolution audio products. Sony is also a leading manufacturer of end-to-end solutions from 4K professional broadcast and A/V equipment to industry leading 4K and 8K Ultra HD TVs.

articles.title_orig: Risk and strategy for Indonesia – China Marine Scientific Research cooperation
articles.title_zh: Risk and strategy for Indonesia – China Marine Scientific Research cooperation
articles.content_orig:
During the Indonesia-China foreign ministers’ meeting in Jakarta in August this year, both countries agreed to make maritime cooperation one of the main pillars of Indonesia-China strategic dialogue. One of the maritime cooperation priority agendas discussed was marine scientific research . But with China often using marine scientific research as part of its assertive maritime strategy , Indonesia should develop a plan to ensure that cooperation in this area will not threaten Indonesia’s security.
In the past few years, China has intensified marine scientific research. According to CSIS , China has more marine scientific research vessels operating in the Indo-Pacific than any other country, including the United States. Chinese research vessels operate in various locations from the South China Sea to the Indian Ocean . So how can Indonesia and China advance marine scientific research that benefits both countries while keeping national security interests in mind?
Indeed, the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) encourages cooperation on marine scientific research to advance human knowledge of the ocean. Given the vastness and depth of the world’s oceans, scientists often consider them largely unexplored. But it is important to note that under UNCLOS, marine scientific research should be conducted for peaceful purposes and should not become the basis for asserting maritime claims.
For Indonesia, the world’s largest archipelagic state with a vast maritime area within its exclusive economic zone and continental shelf, knowledge of what lies beneath its waters is critical. However, with limited technology and resource capacity, international cooperation on marine scientific research is becoming very important.
But despite the benefits that Indonesia may get by conducting marine scientific research cooperation with China, it also carry significant risks. In recent years, China’s research activities have operated illegally in Indonesian waters. For instance, the research vessel Haiyang Dizhi 10 has often conducted illegal surveys in Indonesia’s Exclusive Economic Zone. Moreover, Chinese-owned uncrewed underwater vehicles (UUVs) have also been found operating in Indonesian archipelagic waters.
With these growing concerns, Indonesia should consider three things when developing marine scientific research that can benefit both Indonesia and China.
First, marine scientific research cooperation needs a clear definition and scope. Under UNCLOS, there are no clear definitions of marine scientific research. As a result, different parties interpret for themselves what counts as marine scientific research. A wide range of generally recognized activities include seabed topography, geology, fisheries ecosystems, marine ecosystems, genetic resources, and environmental protection.
Some other activities, despite using some of the same capabilities and data collection methods, are usually not regarded as marine scientific research. For instance, surveillance for military purposes or survey activities for oil and gas exploration are often considered not part of academic marine scientific research.
When it comes to cooperation with China, however, this scope of research can be difficult to distinguish, particularly because of the strong link between Chinese research institutions and the People’s Liberation Army. Some reports suggest that Chinese university-based research institutions supply research to the PLA . Such a close relationship may expose Indonesia’s marine data and spatial information to Chinese military institutions.
Therefore, the cooperation agreement between Indonesia and China should clearly define what activities qualify as marine scientific research and how the data may be used.
Secondly, all cooperation projects should comply with UNCLOS jurisdictional regulations. For instance, marine scientific research in the EEZ, archipelagic waters, and territorial waters should be based on the consent of coastal states. Under UNCLOS, this consent has to be specific to each research project. Indonesia therefore should maintain the requirement to secure its consent for each research activity conducted in its maritime areas under the cooperation agreement.
In the past five years alone, at least three Chinese UUVs were found in Indonesian archipelagic waters in Lombok and South Sulawesi, accidentally discovered by local Indonesian fishermen. Chinese research institutions allegedly operated these UUVs without consent and permission from the Indonesian authorities. Therefore, those UUVs operated in Indonesian waters illegally and cannot be considered legitimate.
Moreover, the type of scientific research conducted and where it is conducted can sometimes be contested. For instance, in research related to hydrography and military activities, coastal states and major maritime powers often disagree. The United States and the United Kingdom consider hydrography and military research to be allowed within the EEZ, and reject efforts by coastal states with more restrictive policies to regulate such research.
Marine scientific research can also be sensitive, particularly in a contested maritime area. For instance, even though Indonesia does not recognize any overlapping maritime claim with China, Indonesia’s EEZ overlaps with China’s illegal nine-dash line. Therefore, any research activity conducted in the overlapping area could also become very sensitive.
Thirdly, it is important to have a reciprocal agreement between Indonesian and Chinese research institutions. It should not only allow Chinese institutions to conduct research in Indonesian waters, but also allow Indonesian scholars and researchers to conduct research in Chinese waters and access information from that research.
This reciprocal agreement could not only give Indonesian research institutions more data and information, but it could also increase the possibility of technology transfer for Indonesian researchers and institutions.
Marine scientific research cooperation between Indonesia and China is important for both countries. However, given China’s aggressive maritime behavior, which often uses marine scientific research to assert its aggressive and illegal claims, Indonesia should ensure any such cooperation follows these principles so that it is not co-opted to serve China’s interests.
Cover photo: Cen Yunpeng/Xinhua/Getty Images
Aristyo Rizka Darmawan is an Assistant Professor of international law at Universitas Indonesia and a PhD Scholar at the Australian National University.

articles.title_orig: Darryl M. Bell and Kadeem Hardison Reunite for New Black Effect Podcast, “A Different World View” - iHeartMedia, Inc.
articles.title_zh: Darryl M. Bell and Kadeem Hardison Reunite for New Black Effect Podcast, “A Different World View” - iHeartMedia, Inc.
articles.content_orig:
The longtime friends and co-stars bring nearly 40 years of chemistry to the mic for an episode-by-episode rewatch, plus candid conversations on entertainment, pop culture, sports and more
Legendary “A Different World” producer and director Debbie Allen to join the series as its first guest
NEW YORK – OCTOBER 8, 2026 – iHeartMedia and Charlamagne Tha God’s Black Effect Podcast Network today announced “A Different World View with Darryl & Kadeem,” a new weekly rewatch podcast hosted by Kadeem Hardison and Darryl M. Bell. The series will premiere Thursday, October 15, with new episodes available every Thursday on the iHeartRadio app and wherever podcasts are heard.
Nearly four decades after becoming Dwayne Wayne and Ron Johnson on the groundbreaking sitcom “A Different World,” Hardison and Bell are back together and behind the mic. Each week, the pair will bring their nearly 40-year friendship and signature chemistry to conversations spanning entertainment, pop culture, sports and whatever else has their attention before heading back to Hillman. They’ll rewatch “A Different World” episode by episode, sharing behind-the-scenes stories, unpacking why the groundbreaking series continues to resonate nearly four decades later and welcoming familiar faces from the show along the way. They’ll also look ahead to the new Netflix sequel series, with conversations featuring members of both the original and new casts.
Debbie Allen will join Hardison and Bell as the podcast’s first guest, as the pair kicks off their rewatch with Season 2, Episode 2, Allen’s first episode with the series. Together, they’ll revisit how Allen came to “A Different World,” her early connection with Hardison and Bell and the transformation of the series under her leadership, while also looking ahead to the road that brought Hillman back for a new generation. Allen also serves as an executive producer on the Netflix sequel series, directs its premiere episode and appears as Dr. Langhorne.
“I am beyond excited to finally launch the ‘A Different World View with Darryl and Kadeem’ podcast,” said Bell. “Kadeem and I have only wanted to do this for over 25 years, and the time is now! I also could not be happier or think of better partners than Charlamagne Tha God, his team at The Black Effect and iHeartMedia.”
Kadeem Hardison and Darryl M. Bell are best known for their iconic roles as Dwayne Wayne and Ron Johnson Jr. on “A Different World.” Their careers have spanned film, television and production, with the pair first appearing together in Spike Lee’s “School Daze.” In recent years, they have reunited with their former castmates for the “A Different World” historically Black colleges and universities tour, celebrating the series’ lasting impact with a new generation of students. Hardison and Bell will also reprise their roles in the new sequel series.
“‘A Different World’ had an undeniable impact on Black culture, and Kadeem and Darryl are such an important part of that legacy,” said Dollie S. Bishop, President of The Black Effect Podcast Network. “We’re excited to give them a platform to bring their friendship and comedy to listeners everywhere, sharing stories fans have never heard and celebrating the series with the generations who grew up with it and those who might just be discovering it today.”
“I’ve been talking to this guy for 40 years,” said Hardison. “I’m so glad you all get to see what I’ve been dealing with. ‘A Different World View’ coming shortly!”
“A Different World View with Darryl & Kadeem” is distributed by iHeartPodcasts and is part of the Black Effect Podcast Network. Listen to the official trailer HERE . Beginning October 15, new episodes will be available every Thursday on the iHeartRadio app and wherever podcasts are heard. Video episodes will also be available on YouTube.
About Black Effect Podcast Network
The Black Effect Podcast Network is a transformative network founded by renowned cultural architect, executive producer, bestselling author and media mogul Charlamagne Tha God in a historic joint venture with the world’s No. 1 commercial podcast publisher, iHeartMedia. Charlamagne and iHeartMedia created the groundbreaking first-ever Black Effect Podcast Network, celebrating the essential Black culture-shapers on the planet—in education, entertainment, politics, pop culture, and sports. The Black Effect Podcast Network gives rise to emerging and established content creators and storytellers whose perspectives and creative visions have been marginalized and overlooked while serving an audience that has been underserved. The Black Effect Podcast Network helps its partners define their place in podcast culture through influence, ideas, and experiences that engage, inspire, inform and empower.

articles.title_orig: Pope Leo's Vatican II Catechesis 27: The Mission of the Church in the Contemporary World
articles.title_zh: Pope Leo's Vatican II Catechesis 27: The Mission of the Church in the Contemporary World
articles.content_orig:
Pope Leo XIV speaks to visitors during his weekly general audience in St. Peter’s Square at the Vatican Oct. 7. Photo by CNS photo/Vatican Media
On Wednesday, Jan. 7, Pope Leo XIV announced that he would begin a new series of talks dedicated to the documents of the Second Vatican Council during his weekly general audiences. The Second Vatican Council, also known as Vatican II, was held from Oct. 11, 1962, through Dec. 8, 1965.
Pope Leo delivered the 27th installment of his catechesis, available below, on Wednesday, Oct. 7, in St. Peter's Square at the Vatican.
Brothers and sisters, good morning and welcome!
Resuming our reflection on the Conciliar Constitution Gaudium et Spes, today we will consider the fourth chapter of the first part, dedicated to the Church’s mission in the contemporary world.
First of all, the Council recalls that the Church is not “above” or “beside” the world, but is, as it were, grafted into it. “Mundus reconciliatus Ecclesia”, wrote St. Augustine (Sermon 96): the Church is the world already reconciled with God; we are pilgrims on earth and share in this world’s fragility and beauty (cf. GS, 40).
Just as the Son of God was incarnated to give life to the world and to reconcile it with the Father, so the Church dwells in the world as a sign of the incarnation of God, in order to manifest His plan to make us all His children in one great human family. Therefore, the Church journeys through history in the midst of peoples and cultures, and “this involvement in people’s lives helps the Church understand ever more clearly that her mission has a historical scope and entails a responsibility for the way in which social relations are built” (Encyclical Letter Magnifica Humanitas , 19).
The first mission of the Church is to help people be attentive to the profound questions of life: those concerning our origin and our destiny, as well as those concerning the meaning of love and suffering (cf. GS, 41). The logic of profit at all costs and the manipulation of information risk exerting undue pressure on people to conform to a lifestyle centered on the consumption of material goods, but our hearts are made to look upwards.
The Council Fathers remind us that the Church’s mission is fulfilled also in contributing to the construction of the earthly city. However, her methods and aims are not primarily of a political order; rather, they consist in bearing witness to faith and charity, together with commitment for justice, peace, and fraternity. By worshipping Christ, the Righteous One who died for the unrighteous, the believer cannot accept the oppression of the weak and the poor, nor the unjust structures that perpetuate conditions of dependence and injustice. The social doctrine of the Church guides the actions of Christians, who collaborate with all people of good will in promoting the common good. The Church, therefore, “has no fiercer desire than that in pursuit of the welfare of all she may be able to develop herself freely under any kind of government which grants recognition to the basic rights of person and family, to the demands of the common good” (GS, 42).
To fulfil the Gospel mission effectively, it is necessary for every baptized person to commit to cooperating with the grace of the Holy Spirit, so that their faith may be living and expressed in consistent behavior. Indeed, as the Council Fathers reiterate, the discrepancy between professed faith and daily life “deserves to be counted among the more serious errors of our age” (GS, 43).
Gaudium et Spes reserves special mention (cf. ibid.) for the mission of the lay faithful who, by virtue of their Baptism, are called to enliven the world with the Christian spirit and the vision of the Gospel. The principal settings for this activity, which may well be described as priestly, are undoubtedly the family and the workplace, but it extends to every sphere of life.
Finally, the Church is always attentive to what is taking place and developing in society (cf. GS, 44). It is the task of the whole People of God, especially pastors and theologians, to discern what in the cultures of our time is worthy of consideration, always taking the Word of God and the Tradition of the Church as the supreme criteria for discernment. This requires a balanced mind, free from cultural trends, capable of viewing the world in a positive light whilst remaining steadfast in preserving and presenting the Gospel message in its entirety. Indeed, “it is certainly not by watering down the content or softening the demands that Christianity can be made attractive” (Address to the Plenary Assembly of the Dicastery for Evangelization – Section on Fundamental Questions regarding Evangelization in the World, 28 May 2026).
Dear friends, as she journeys through history, “the Church has a single intention: that God’s kingdom may come, and that the salvation of the whole human race may come to pass” (GS, 45). She strives towards this end above all through personal holiness and fraternal love. St. Paul VI wrote: “Without this mark of holiness, our word will have difficulty in touching the heart of modern man. It risks being vain and sterile” (Apostolic Exhortation Evangelii Nuntiandi, 76). Let us therefore be open to the action of the Holy Spirit, that He may help us to live in holiness and charity, so that the world may believe and hope.

articles.title_orig: Trump's foreign worker crackdown comes for Microsoft, Adobe, IT firms
articles.title_zh: Trump's foreign worker crackdown comes for Microsoft, Adobe, IT firms
articles.content_orig:
The U.S. Department of Labor announced it would suspend Microsoft and Adobe from its Permanent Labor Certification program on Thursday, Labor Secretary Keith Sonderling said, as the Trump administration continues to take aim at immigration and foreign hiring programs ahead of November's midterm elections.
Sonderling said the Labor Department won't accept or process any new applications under the program for a host of companies, including Cognizant, Infosys, Capgemini, Tata, Wipro and HCL.
The secretary said Adobe and Microsoft were also suspended "due to multiple active federal investigations."
"Since 2009, just these companies alone have requested almost 3 million foreign workers. They've received over 230,000 H-1B visas approvals and over 100,000 permanent labor certifications. That's hundreds of thousands of jobs that were taken from American workers," Sonderling said.
Vice President JD Vance criticized Microsoft specifically, pointing to the firm's 6,000 layoffs in 2025. Vance claimed that the company "replaced" those workers with people on H-1B visas.
"So we're going to continue to support Microsoft and have a great relationship with Microsoft, but we're also going to deny them the ability to apply for these permanent residencies until they show that they are going to get serious about putting American workers first," Vance said.
President Donald Trump is set to award the National Medal of Science to Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella and other leading technology CEOs on Thursday at the same summit where the suspension announcement was made.
Nadella is from India and moved to the U.S. in 1988. He joined Microsoft in 1992.
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, SpaceXAI CEO Elon Musk and Advanced Micro Devices CEO Lisa Su are also being honored at Thursday's medal ceremony. Each of the leaders immigrated to the U.S. Musk was born in South Africa and Su and Huang were born in Taiwan.
"It's one thing if you want to bring in a person like Elon Musk," Vance said. "I think 99% of American citizens look at somebody like Elon Musk or Lisa Su, the CEO of AMD, and they say, obviously, if that person wants to come in and build something great in the United States of America, we support that."
CNBC has reached out to Microsoft and Adobe for comment.

articles.title_orig: Hurricane Isaias forecast to bring dangerous storm surge, with millions under warnings in US
articles.title_zh: Hurricane Isaias forecast to bring dangerous storm surge, with millions under warnings in US
articles.content_orig:
Residents in areas from the mouth of the Mississippi River to Florida urged to ‘evacuate if told to do so’
Millions of people from Louisiana to Florida are under hurricane warnings on Thursday as Hurricane Isaias looked set to head towards the US Gulf coast with weather officials warning of dangerous storm surge, hurricane-force winds, heavy rainfall, and flooding.
Isaias intensified into a hurricane from a tropical storm on Wednesday night, becoming the first hurricane of the 2026 Atlantic hurricane season.
In an advisory on Thursday morning, the National Weather Service (NWS) said that Isaias, which is currently a category 1 hurricane with sustained winds of 85mph with higher gusts, is expected to pass to the north of the Yucatán peninsula later on Thursday before reaching the northern Gulf coast where it is expected to make landfall late Friday or early Saturday.
The NWS said that Isaias is “expected to strengthen and be a strong hurricane when it approaches the northern Gulf Coast on Friday” and warned that a “life-threatening storm surge” is expected along a portion of the northern Gulf coast.
Storm surge warnings, which are issued when there is a “danger of life-threatening indundation from rising water moving inland from the coastline”, are in effect on Thursday from the mouth of the Mississippi River to Steinhatchee, Florida , and residents in the warning area have been urged to “follow advice given by local officials and evacuate if told to do so”.
Hurricane warnings, meaning that hurricane conditions are expected, are also in effect in the areas from Ocean Springs, Mississippi to the Bay/Gulf county line, Florida. The NWS has warned that “damaging hurricane force-winds are expected over portions of the Florida Panhandle, southern Alabama, and southern Mississippi” and urged residents to prepare for the possibility of “long-duration power outages”.
The NWS warned on Thursday: “Gusty winds are possible in portions of the Yucatan Peninsula today.”
Isaias is also expected to bring “areas of heavy rainfall” to the central Gulf coast and much of the south-east from Friday into the weekend, and the NWS said that flash and urban flooding, along with isolated river flooding, will be possible. From Friday through the weekend, Isaias is expected to produce rainfall amounts of three to seven inches across the central US Gulf coast extending from far south-eastern Louisiana to the Florida Big Bend region.
“Localized totals up to 15 inches are possible, particularly within banding across the Florida Panhandle and Big Bend,” the NWS said.
Isolated tornadoes are also possible on Friday night in coastal areas of Alabama and the Florida Panhandle and far southwestern Georgia, the NWS said, adding that “the tornado threat will continue Saturday for eastern Alabama, Georgia and northern Florida.”
On Wednesday, the Alabama governor, Kay Ivey, declared a state of emergency in 40 counties, saying that the order “will allow us to take any needed steps ahead of landfall”. The emergency declaration is scheduled to remain in effect until 14 October.
The Florida governor, Ron DeSantis, also declared a state of emergency this week for 25 counties as the state prepares.
“This order ensures communities have the time and resources necessary to prepare for potential severe weather impacts to the Panhandle and Big Bend region of Florida,” DeSantis said in the announcement.
At the local level, officials in Okaloosa county, Florida, declared a local state of emergency on Wednesday and ordered some residents in coastal areas to evacuate. Panama City also declared a local state of emergency “due to the potential effects of Isaias and its near threat to the citizens and property in Panama City and surrounding communities”.
Several school districts in Alabama and Florida have also announced closures ahead of Isaias.
The Federal Aviation Administration also warned on Thursday that Isaias may “lead to Gulf route closures”.
In Tennessee, the NWS office in Morristown warned that “remnants of Hurricane Isaias will bring heavy rain and strong, gusty winds to our area this weekend.” The office said that “high winds could top 60–70+ mph in the eastern TN mountains and foothills, with isolated flash flooding possible in heavy rainfall areas.”

articles.title_orig: Health officials report 74 new measles cases in Pennsylvania - ABC News
articles.title_zh: Health officials report 74 new measles cases in Pennsylvania - ABC News
articles.source: Breaking News, Latest News and Videos
articles.content_orig:
Five people have died in the state so far this year.
Pennsylvania is reporting 74 new measles cases since Monday, the state's health department said Wednesday.
A total of 1,078 cases have been reported in the state so far this year. At least 207 people have been hospitalized and five people have died, according to the Pennsylvania Department of Health (DOH) .
"Of the 74 cases added, more than 40 represent individuals who were sick more than two weeks ago and are no longer contagious, but their cases were only recently reported and subsequently confirmed, the DOH said. Wednesday's update "does not reflect a current surge in new infections."
Of the five people who died, two of the deaths were among unvaccinated adults: an 18-year-old and a 40-year-old. The other two deaths were among infants who were too young to have received the measles, mumps, rubella (MMR) vaccine.
The fifth death occurred in an unvaccinated resident of Lancaster County, in southeastern Pennsylvania, but it is unclear how old the individual is. Lancaster County is the epicenter of the state's outbreak, with 401 cases confirmed so far.
One-third of cases are among those under 18 years old and fewer than 1% of cases are among those fully vaccinated with the MMR shot, according to DOH data.
The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention recommends that people receive two doses of the MMR vaccine, the first at ages 12 to 15 months and the second between 4 and 6 years old. One dose is 93% effective in preventing measles infection and two doses are 97% effective, the CDC says.
Infants aged 6 to 11 months living in or traveling to high-risk outbreak areas may receive an early third dose of the MMR vaccine.
CDC data, however shows vaccination rates have been lagging in recent years. During the 2025-26 school year, 92.4% of kindergartners received the MMR vaccine, according to data. This is lower than the 95.2% seen in the 2019-20 school year, prior to the COVID-19 pandemic.
"State health center staff have administered more than 5,700 MMR vaccinations at 198 pop-up vaccination clinics in the affected communities since the outbreak began in late April," DOH wrote in a press release on Wednesday.
"Dozens of additional vaccine clinics are scheduled for the upcoming weeks and months, based on community interest and need," the press release continued. "In pop-up clinics and at state health centers combined, Department nurses have administered nearly 9,000 MMR vaccine doses to residents across the Commonwealth in 2026."

articles.title_orig: Cyborg Politics 3.0: AI and the Algorithms of Unpeace
articles.title_zh: Cyborg Politics 3.0: AI and the Algorithms of Unpeace
articles.content_orig:
https://doi.org/10.60965/bq31-tt86
Today’s debate about the perils and promises of artificial superintelligence is at once terrifyingly existential and astonishingly narrow. It is framed as a good vs. evil binary over humanity’s future: superabundant Utopia or humanity’s extinction. No-one can put a number on the probability of any outcome because the titans of Silicon Valley are accelerating into the unknown.
In this essay, author Alex de Waal argues that this framing misses what has already happened. AI has changed how we think, as members of a social-political collective. AI has hacked the operating system of society and is defining the questions to be posed and limiting the range of allowable answers to those questions.

articles.title_orig: China’s central bank details its view on RMB’s exchange rate
articles.title_zh: China’s central bank details its view on RMB’s exchange rate
articles.content_orig:
Apparently responding to international pressure, the People’s Bank of China, China’s central bank, on October 8 took the rare step of publishing a dedicated article laying out its official stance on RMB exchange rate policy,
The RMB exchange rate, as an important price in the financial market, has been a subject of attention for a lot of people, with increasing discussions recently. Against this backdrop, the People’s Bank of China (PBOC) hereby shares its view on the RMB exchange rate as follows:
● China adopts a managed floating exchange rate regime based on market supply and demand with reference to a basket of currencies. Market forces play a decisive role in determining the RMB exchange rate.
● The RMB exchange rate has floated in both directions over the past two decades. It has experienced several cycles of appreciation and depreciation since 2010, with more pronounced two-way floating and greater flexibility.
● China’s trade growth is driven by its growing industrial competitiveness in the global market. China has no need or intent to gain competitive advantages through currency devaluation, nor has it ever resorted to competitive devaluation.
● Exchange rate dynamics are driven by a number of factors including economic growth, monetary policy, financial market, geopolitics and sudden shocks. There is no straightforward relationship between exchange rate and current account.
● There is no well-established methodology for evaluating the equilibrium level of exchange rates internationally. Therefore, citing idiosyncratic assessment findings as “official evidence” for RMB undervaluation is a misinterpretation and misuse of those findings.
● Global economic imbalances are deeply intertwined with shifting global division of labor, inherent flaws in the international monetary system, and persistently high fiscal deficit and high consumption in some countries. Addressing global imbalances requires collective actions from all stakeholders. Attributing one’s decline in industrial competitiveness, weakened fiscal discipline, and complicated structural issues simply to others’ exchange rates is nothing but shifting the responsibility for adjustment onto others and dodging accountability.
● China has long been a contributor to global economic rebalancing. During the 15 th Five-Year Plan period, China will stay the course in transforming its economic growth model, expand domestic demand, improve business environment, deepen the high-standard opening up, and pursue a more open, inclusive and balanced global economy.
Ⅰ.China’s exchange rate regime
The market-oriented reform of the RMB exchange rate regime is an important part of China’s efforts to build a socialist market economy. China has a firm and consistent commitment to advancing the reform. The Third Plenary Session of the 14 th Central Committee of the Communist Party of China (CPC) in 1993 proposed establishing a managed floating exchange rate regime based on market supply and demand. The Third Plenary Session of the 16 th CPC Central Committee in 2003 called for improving the RMB exchange rate formation mechanism. In 2005, China deepened the market-oriented reform of the RMB exchange rate formation mechanism, and then in 2013, the Third Plenary Session of the 18 th CPC Central Committee made important arrangements for further improving it. As China is a major economy, a market-oriented exchange rate mechanism is aligned with China’s strategic interests and development needs, and also provides solid support for enhancing monetary policy autonomy and effectiveness.
China adopts a managed floating exchange rate regime based on market supply and demand with reference to a basket of currencies. This regime has the following features:
First, market forces play a decisive role in determining the exchange rate. After years of development, a fully functional multi-tiered foreign exchange (FX) market has gradually taken shape in China, with growing market depth and breadth. Market participants take part in FX trading based on commercial considerations and their own judgment. Market supply and demand plays a decisive role in determining the RMB exchange rate. The PBOC maintains exchange rate flexibility and two-way floating. It neither targets a specific level for the RMB exchange rate, nor seeks to determine its longer-term trajectory. The PBOC has phased out regular intervention in the FX market since 2017.
Second, the focus is laid upon preventing short-term fluctuations in the exchange rate from undermining financial stability, in particular sharp depreciation within a short time. Under certain circumstances where exogenous shocks hit the country, such as the sudden outbreak of the pandemic and the tariff war in April 2025, the PBOC will use macroprudential tools to guide expectations, or even market interventions in extreme cases, to correct herd behavior and irrational market expectations, in particular the self-reinforcing irrational expectations for depreciation, to prevent disruptive short-term overshooting of the exchange rate.
Such measures are consistent with international rules and practices. For example, during the 2008 global financial crisis, some emerging economies experienced sharp fluctuations in their currencies, so they intervened in the market to stop excessive currency depreciation from triggering financial risks. In July 2026, the Japanese yen hit its 40-year low against the US dollar, prompting joint intervention by relevant countries.
Third, the exchange rate policy has become more transparent. Since its subscription to the International Monetary Fund’s (IMF) Special Data Dissemination Standard (SDDS) in 2015, China has released balance of payments and related foreign exchange data in line with higher international standards, with greater granularity and higher frequency. In response to the IMF’s call for greater transparency, China will start reporting foreign exchange operation data to the IMF in 2027.
Ⅱ.RMB exchange rate movements
The RMB has moved in both directions since the exchange rate regime reform in 2005, and has remained strong among peers. In bilateral terms, the RMB has strengthened against the US dollar from 8.27 per dollar in July 2005, when the reform was launched, to around 6.7 per dollar recently, appreciating by 23 percent cumulatively. In multilateral terms, the RMB nominal effective exchange rate (NEER) calculated by the Bank for International Settlements (BIS) has appreciated by over 50 percent since the exchange rate regime reform in 2005, while its real effective exchange rate (REER) up by 35 percent.
The RMB exchange rate has experienced several cycles of appreciation and depreciation since 2010, with more pronounced two-way floating and greater flexibility. The RMB went through three appreciation-depreciation cycles against the US dollar, trading broadly within the range of 6.04 to 7.35 per dollar. In each cycle, the magnitude of change, be it to the upside or downside, both exceeded 10 percent.
The RMB exchange rate has floated in both directions and appreciated in an orderly manner since 2025. The RMB has strengthened by about 9 percent against the US dollar since 2025. In particular, while non-dollar currencies have weakened broadly amid surging US dollar index and Treasury yields since 2026, the RMB has extended its upward trend against the dollar. Looking forward, the RMB exchange rate is shaped by a diverse array of drivers. There are both factors pushing for appreciation and depreciation, and there are still uncertainties surrounding the RMB’s trajectory.
Ⅲ. China has no need or intent to gain trade competitive advantages through currency devaluation
China’s trade growth is driven by its growing industrial competitiveness in the global market. In history, most major surplus countries boasted strong industrial competitiveness. articles.title_orig: Genre-defying Canadian poet Anne Carson wins 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature
articles.title_zh: Genre-defying Canadian poet Anne Carson wins 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature
articles.content_orig:
Most prestigious literature prize goes to Canadian known for genre-crossing works such as Autobiography of Red
The Nobel prize in literature has been awarded to the Canadian poet and essayist Anne Carson, the Swedish Academy has announced.
The academy cited the author’s “bold and inventive oeuvre that, in playful dialogue with the classical tradition, has created new forms for contemporary literature”.
The Nobel prize, regarded as the most prestigious award in global literature, is awarded for a lifetime body of work. The winner receives 12m Swedish kronor (£900,000).
Ingrid Carlberg, the permanent secretary of the Swedish Academy, said she had told Carson of the award on the phone shortly before the news broke. “She had time to tell me that she is, for the moment, in Iceland, where she is listening to the wind,” Carlberg said. “She was taken by surprise but very happy. I could hear that in her voice.”
Born in Toronto in 1950, Carson is known for work that moves freely between poetry, prose and translation , drawing heavily on the literature and mythology of the ancient Greek world. She has been a professor of classics at various institutions including Princeton, New York University and McGill University in Montreal. She is the 19th woman to win, out of 123 literature laureates.
Carson’s first book, Eros the Bittersweet, was published in 1986 and combined literary criticism with an exploration of desire and the ancient Greek tradition.
Her best-known work is Autobiography of Red, a 1998 novel in verse inspired by the fragments of the ancient Greek poet Stesichorus. It reimagines the myth of Geryon, the red-winged monster killed by Herakles, as the story of a modern teenage boy navigating heartbreak and desire.
In 2001, she became the first woman to win the TS Eliot prize, for her collection The Beauty of the Husband. She has also been awarded Guggenheim and MacArthur fellowships.
The Canadian prime minister, Mark Carney, congratulated the poet on X after the announcement. “With wit, imagination, and a style entirely her own, Canadian poet Anne Carson has reimagined the classics. She has brought ancient stories to new audiences and transformed the way we think about literature,” he said, adding that it was a “proud moment for Canada”.
David Leonard, the executive director of the Writers’ Trust of Canada , said: “Anne is such a brilliant writer. Her work is broad, but also extremely smart.” Calling Carson’s work “intoxicating”, he said her four-decade career had resulted in a peerless collection of poems and essays. “They’re beautiful, they’re smart, they’re true and they are humane. It’s exactly what we need in our writing.”
Carson’s work has attracted praise from fellow writers including Susan Sontag, who once said: “She is one of the few writers writing in English that I would read anything she wrote. If there’s a magazine that has something of hers in it, I buy it automatically.”
Anders Olsson, the chair of the Swedish Academy’s Nobel Committee for Literature, praised Carson for work that had “broken away from lyrical poetry bound to the narrative self and inspired new forms of contemporary literature”. He said: “This method of writing leads to playful and ironic works that move not only between classical and modern poetry but also between different genres and artforms.”
Carson’s books have ranged widely in form. Men in the Off Hours combined verse essays, poems, epitaphs and prose about artists and historical figures, and won the inaugural Griffin poetry prize in 2001. Decreation, another eclectic work, brought together poetry, essays and an opera.
Nox, published in 2010, is particularly characteristic of Carson’s avant-garde approach to literature – the book takes the form of an accordion-fold box containing a reproduction of a notebook Carson made after the death of her brother. Her later works include Red Doc> and Float.
In a Guardian review of Red Doc>, Sarah Crown wrote: “To engage so fluidly, so originally and compellingly, with a story first told more than 3,000 years ago, is astonishing: her ambition is one thing; the fact that it is so completely achieved is, frankly, something else.”
Much of Carson’s work has emerged from her fascination with language itself. The Swedish Academy noted: “Almost all her literary production has centred upon the intersection between the philologist’s obsession with words and the poet’s desire for new meaning,” adding that Carson had identified the etymology of words as “the starting point for all her work”.
Asked why she continually moved between forms, Carson said in an interview: “Boredom, I guess. There is a restlessness. There are a lot of forms to try.”
She has acknowledged the difficulties that come with her experimental style. “[My work] does fall apart a lot,” she said in a 2018 interview. “It gets just too weird for anyone to care about reading, or else it gets diluted into a sort of parody of itself.”
Ira Wells, the president of PEN Canada, said Carson’s win felt “particularly significant at a moment in which Canada and Europe are strengthening cultural ties amidst broader global disruption”. He added: “On an aesthetic level, Carson’s verse vibrates on profound human frequencies, at a moment in which more and more language is formulated by machines.”
Carson has generally kept her personal life out of interviews. However, in an August 2024 article for the London Review of Books, she disclosed that she had been diagnosed with Parkinson’s disease.
The Nobel prize in literature has been awarded on 118 previous occasions since 1901. Recent laureates include Annie Ernaux, Bob Dylan, Abdulrazak Gurnah, Louise Glück, Peter Handke and Olga Tokarczuk. Last year’s recipient was the Hungarian author László Krasznahorkai, known for his dystopic and avant-garde writing.
Carson, 76, will formally receive the medal and diploma in a ceremony in Stockholm in December.
To browse works by Anne Carson, visit guardianbookshop.com . Delivery charges may apply.

Aims to Provide One Million Meals to Children in Need
NEW YORK, NY / ACCESS Newswire / October 8, 2026 / TABLE FOR TWO USA (TFT) invites everyone to participate in the 12th Annual ONIGIRI ACTION that will run from Thursday, October 8 to Tuesday, November 17, 2026 to provide one million school meals to children in need. During the campaign, through the generosity of our partner organizations (see below), every rice ball related post to the campaign website or social media with #OnigiriAction will provide five school meals to children in need. TFT will enhance school meals in socioeconomically disadvantaged neighborhoods in the U.S. by adding fresh vegetables and fruits to school lunches. TFT will additionally provide school meals to children in East Africa.
Our ONIGIRI ACTION campaign commemorates United Nations' World Food Day. As a nonprofit organization with roots in Japan, the campaign highlights onigiri (rice balls), which are a traditional Japanese comfort food made with love to share with others.
Since its launch in 2015, ONIGIRI ACTION has supported over twelve million school meals. TABLE FOR TWO has additionally received two prestigious awards: one related to Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) and the other for health and culture from the Japanese government ( https://bit.ly/3Kg0ZHY ). Amid rising food prices driven by climate change, geopolitical instability, and ongoing global economic uncertainty, concerns are growing that Zero Hunger, one of the Sustainable Development Goals, will not be achieved. As these pressures continue to mount, the need for TFT to deliver healthy meals to those in need becomes more critical every year.
TFT and our partners will host numerous virtual and in-person events to celebrate ONIGIRI ACTION. Through onigiri, we can have meaningful connections and shared cultural experiences. Together with Japanese consulates across the United States, we are organizing the Onigiri Diplomacy Project. Consulates will post photos with #OnigiriAction, display the campaign poster and props, and in some cases organize an interactive onigiri experience or event. We will additionally run Intercollege Onigiri Action, a fun and collaborative initiative on Instagram for college students in the U.S. The group with the most onigiri posts will win, and special awards will also be given for the most creative reel and best group photo. There will also be special Nationwide Shared Table hybrid cooking event supported by Japan Foundation New York where participants nationwide will learn how to make creative and delicious onigiri.
Event information and updates will be announced on our website and social media .
Partner Organizations in the U.S.: For every onigiri photo posted, five school meals will be provided through the generous support of our partners: J.C.C. Fund/Japanese Chamber of Commerce and Industry of New York, JFC International/Nishiki, JCAW, Zojirushi America, San-J, ITOCHU International & ITOCHU Europe, SMBC Americas Foundation, Misuzu Corporation, MUFG Bank, Mishima Foods U.S.A., Kewpie Americas, and Six Tree Foundation. Onigiri partners: BentOn, Onigilly, Sunny Blue, Omusubee
To Learn More: ONIGIRI ACTION (USA site): https://usa.tablefor2.org/onigiri-action ONIGIRI ACTION (Global site): https://onigiri-action.com/en/
Products with Donations: During the campaign, a portion of the proceeds from products below will be donated to provide school meals: Nishiki rice (JFC International), rice cookers (Zojirushi America), tamari soy sauce (San-J), Tamaki Gold (ITOCHU International), inari (Misuzu Corporation), nori komi furikake (Mishima Foods U.S.A.), KEWPIE mayonnaise (Kewpie Americas), okonomiyaki pancake mix (Otafuku Foods).
About TABLE FOR TWO USA: TFT is a 501(c)(3) organization that addresses hunger and health issues caused by unhealthy eating by educating people about healthy eating habits and providing nutritious school meals to those in need. TABLE FOR TWO started in Japan and now operates globally. As one of the most well-known NPOs in Japan, a country celebrated for the longevity of its people, TFT USA promotes Japanese healthy eating culture and has launched innovative programs, ONIGIRI ACTION, Wa-Sho - Learn. Cook. Eat Japanese! - and Edamame Champ, featuring Japanese food culture to tackle critical health issues.

articles.title_orig: Harvard celebrates World Mental Health Week
articles.title_zh: Harvard celebrates World Mental Health Week
articles.content_orig:
From October 13-16, 2026 Harvard will host World Mental Health Week , a series of events and activities focused on supporting student mental health and wellbeing. Throughout the week, students can participate in guided meditation sessions, pet therapy sessions, and craft activities such as flower bouquet making and watercolor painting.
The events will take place following World Mental Health Day on Saturday, October 10, 2026. Each year, World Mental Health Day inspires organizations around the world to share resources and plan events in the pursuit of destigmatizing mental health challenges and encouraging the transformation of mental health services. This year’s theme, “ Lived Experiences Heard: Real Voices, Real Change, ” highlights the power of lived experiences in transforming how we approach mental health challenges, develop strategies to address them, and deliver services to those in need.
Schools and departments across the University are collaborating with the Office of the Associate Provost for Student Affairs to sponsor events, including workshops and discussion sessions.
Highlights include a fireside chat sponsored by Harvard Medical School Center for Bioethics, the Harvard Medical School Department of Global Health and Social Medicine, and Countway Library, in which Dr. Vikram Patel, Paul Farmer Professor and chair of Global Health and Social Medicine at Harvard Medical School and Dr. S. Abbas Shobeiri, Division Chief of Benign Gynecology and Director of the Pelvic Floor Program at Inova Health System, will explore trauma and healing and how storytelling and art can help approach mental health differently.
Another highlight includes a seminar at the Lee Kum Sheung Center for Health and Happiness at the Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health with Dr. Lauren Taylor, assistant professor of Population Health at the NYU Grossman School of Medicine, which will explore the role of trust in healthcare delivery.
Find a listing of all activities, as well as strategies, tools, and resources for maintaining or improving mental health at: https://www.harvard.edu/wellbeing/.
In addition to the services available from Harvard’s Counseling and Mental Health Services (CAMHS) and the Center for Wellness and Health Promotion (CWHP), students can access mental health providers and services through TimelyCare, a virtual health and wellbeing platform, designed to expand access to no-cost mental health and wellness services for registered students.

articles.title_orig: Warrants to Search Former Prince Andrew’s Properties Were Unlawful, Court Says
articles.title_zh: Warrants to Search Former Prince Andrew’s Properties Were Unlawful, Court Says
articles.content_orig:
Thames Valley Police has accepted warrants it used to search Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor's homes at the time of his arrest in February were unlawful, the High Court was told.
Following Thursday's hearing, items seized in the raids continue to be held by the police for now, and the criminal investigation into Mountbatten-Windsor is continuing.
The former prince, who denies any wrongdoing, was arrested by police on 19 February on suspicion of misconduct in public office, after which he launched a legal challenge over the legality of the search warrants.
The force said it accepted that the "initial court's decision to issue warrants under the specific piece of legislation used was incorrect" before they searched the properties.
On Thursday at the High Court, Judge Mr Justice Hilliard said Mountbatten-Windsor and the police had agreed that the search warrants had been unlawful.
However, he added: "The fact that the search warrants were quashed does not bring the investigation to an end or mean that the whole of the investigation is unlawful."
Mountbatten-Windsor opposes the police's bid to retain the evidence, the judge said, and another hearing is expected in 2027.
His lawyers have used a judicial review to challenge the actions of the force's chief constable and the Central Criminal Court in the build-up to his arrest.
His arrest arose after the US Department of Justice published documents which raised suspicions he had forwarded confidential information to the convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein when Mountbatten-Windsor was a UK trade envoy in 2010.
He has consistently denied any wrongdoing in relation to Epstein.
The court heard on Thursday that Thames Valley Police seized documents and electronic devices when they raided Mountbatten-Windsor's homes earlier this year.
Thames Valley Police's position was that they had applied for search warrants under section eight and nine of the Police and Criminal Evidence Act 1984 at a hearing at the Central Criminal Court the day before the search.
That court determined that only section eight search warrants were needed and they were granted on that basis - but subsequently, a legal challenge has established that the court should have issued them under the section nine.
The judge explained on Thursday why the police could keep hold of the former prince's items that had been seized.
He said: "There would be little point in handing property back if it could then simply be lawfully seized under some other provision."
A Thames Valley Police spokesperson said: "The agreement that led to the quashing of the warrants relates specifically to a decision made by the court regarding the legal basis for these and is not a judgement on our ongoing investigation.
"We ensured the court was presented with all the necessary information and paperwork to inform their decision, following the correct legal processes throughout.
"We accept the position that the initial court's decision to issue warrants under the specific piece of legislation used was incorrect and therefore these must be legally quashed.
"Legal proceedings are currently ongoing to decide how material seized during the searches will be managed and whether we can lawfully retain it in support of our ongoing investigation."
The force said its "investigation into alleged misconduct in public office by a man in his 60s from Norfolk remains ongoing, and we continue to pursue all reasonable lines of enquiry to effectively and fairly progress this investigation".
The next stage in this legal dispute will be a behind-closed-doors hearing over whether the police can still retain material seized from Mountbatten-Windsor's homes under alternative powers designed for situations like this.
The error that has led to Thames Valley Police accepting the search warrants were unlawful relates to the particular power the judge permitted the force to use when its officers raided the properties.
Strict legal safeguards on searches bar the police from automatically seizing sensitive material without thinking through in advance the need to take it.
Examples of that material include advice from a suspect's lawyer or material which does not really belong to them, such as copies of confidential work-related papers from an employer.
In practice, if the police find such material during a search, they should return it rather than use it in their investigation.
The category of search warrant that was granted by the court in this instance did not take into account the possibility of such protected material being seized.
However, the law says police can in fact seize that kind of material - or potentially retain it in the event of an error - providing they pass some extra tests.
Thames Valley Police must now convince a judge that the material is likely to be of "substantial value" to their investigation into Mountbatten-Windsor and, ultimately, potential evidence to present to a court.
So while the force has conceded the search warrant was unlawful, a judge will have to decide whether this alternative search power, with its extra safeguards, justifies them keeping and using the material after all.

articles.title_orig: The Story Behind the Butterfly’s Enhanced Visual World of Color
articles.title_zh: The Story Behind the Butterfly’s Enhanced Visual World of Color
articles.content_orig:
Researchers discovered the genetic switch that produces extra light-detecting cells that led to the ability to recognize more colors in flowers and other butterflies
Many insects see the world through hundreds of tiny lenses that are grouped together in a visual organ known as the compound eye. Behind each lens sits a cluster of eight light-detecting cells arranged in a pattern that scientists believe has existed for hundreds of millions of years.
Butterflies are the rare exception. They are equipped with nine light-detecting cells, which gives them the ability to visually navigate a much richer world of color, compared with insects such as flies, and allows them to locate nectar and potential mates.
University of California San Diego scientists in School of Biological Sciences Associate Professor Michael Perry’s lab have discovered the genetic modification that gave butterflies this visual advantage.
“Butterflies see far more color than flies do because at some point in their evolution they added a photoreceptor to every unit of their compound eye — a rare break from an eye design that has otherwise been conserved across insects for hundreds of millions of years,” said Perry, a faculty member in the Department of Cell and Developmental Biology. “We found the genetic switch that did it.”
In a study published in the journal Science Advances , Perry and his coauthors identified the genetic steps involved in the emergence of the ninth photoreceptor in painted lady butterflies, the most widespread butterfly species in the world. While flies feature light-sensing cells known as photoreceptors R1-R8, butterflies expanded their color vision by adding a second R7 photoreceptor to each unit of the eye, the researchers found. To test whether that genetic change was enough on its own, they recreated it in a fruit fly — switching on a gene in cells that normally keeps it off, and timing it to the brief window when the eye is being built. This produced a “butterfly fly” that grows its eyes on the butterfly plan, with nine cells per eye unit instead of eight.
Antibody stains in a developing butterfly retina show that each unit eye contains two R7 color photoreceptors. Credit: Perry Lab, UC San Diego
A new light detector in the eye would be of no use if the brain is not able to connect to the new information provided by that detector. The scientists assumed that adding a sensory input such as a new photoreceptor unit should require the brain to slowly evolve a matching neuron partner that would receive information on the other end. That didn’t happen, the researchers found. To their surprise, no adaptive change was needed.
The fly brain regularly overproduces neurons that die off if they fail to find a connection. The brain of the butterfly-fly, they found, knew precisely how to handle the new photoreceptor by using its extra “standby” neurons and put them in play.
“When we gave those spare neurons something to connect to, they survived and wired up correctly — immediately — with no further genetic change,” said Perry. “In other words, the brain was ready before the eye asked. This is a rare, concrete case of evolution making use of neurons that were otherwise going to die.”
The new study’s findings provide a glimpse of how insects, with a flexible brain framework, were able to accommodate new inputs to evolutionarily adapt to an emerging need in their environment: an elevated ability to visualize flowering plants.
The team also found a hawkmoth that appears to be partway through the same transition: the lower half of its eye is butterfly-like, with two of these cells per unit, while the upper half is fly-like, with one. That is roughly what you would expect if the change began in one region of the eye and spread.
The research team is now exploring further unanswered questions, such as the difficult-to-study issue of whether the butterfly-fly can in fact see more vivid color with the additional photoreceptor, as butterflies do.
The research team included Ke Gao, Julia Ainsworth, Antoine Donati, Yunchong Zhao, Michelle Franc Ragsac, Cara Genduso, Zoie Andre, Andrew Tomlinson and Michael W. Perry. The researchers acknowledge support from: the National Institutes of Health (1T32GM133351); a Hellman Fellowship (Hellman Fellows Fund); a National Science Foundation CAREER award (2339031); and an NIH National Human Genome Research Institute grant (R01HG013634) from the EDGE program.
