articles.title_orig: Thousands to march in Madrid after death of evicted pensioner Maricarmen
articles.title_zh: Thousands to march in Madrid after death of evicted pensioner Maricarmen
articles.content_orig:
Rally to remember woman, 87, whose rent battle with investment firm triggered nationwide protests over housing crisis
Thousands of people are expected to march through the centre of Madrid on Thursday evening in memory of María del Carmen Abascal, the 87-year-old woman whose eviction from her flat in the capital a fortnight before her death triggered mass protests over Spain’s housing crisis .
The pensioner, whose flat had been bought by an investment firm that sought to increase her rent by 230%, had become the public face of the crisis before her death in hospital on Wednesday night.
Abascal’s eviction unleashed waves of demonstrations across Spain, led to the setting up of a protest camp in the centre of the capital, and prompted the socialist-led government to propose emergency measures to try to make the rental market more equitable. When those measures were voted down by rightwing and far-right parties last week, the prime minister, Pedro Sánchez, announced a snap general election , to be held on 29 November.
Anger over the plight of the woman who had become known around the country as Maricarmen remained undimmed a few hours after her death. On the pavement across from the apartment building where she had lived for seven decades, a steady stream of people visited a small, steadily growing memorial. Some came to light candles or leave flowers, while others left handwritten messages such as, “You made history Maricarmen,” and “Thank you for changing Spain”. Sara, 41, who had come with her young son and a sign that read, “Maricarmen, we’ll fight for you”, said: “We’re here because I think Maricarmen’s death shows how institutions can kill a person by failing to care for them.”
For many, the site was a reminder of all that Maricarmen had gone through as she tried to stay in her home, fending off three eviction attempts before the investment firm succeeded in forcing her out. “When people are protected less than investors, that leads to these kinds of things happening,” Sara added. “This woman could have died – if she had died of natural causes – she could have died peacefully in her home.”
Jaime, 34, pointed to all that Maricarmen had come to represent, particularly in a country like Spain, where social rights are supposedly guaranteed. “She had become a symbol, albeit one she never wanted to be, of the fight for decent housing,” he said. “So I came here because I think it’s important to restore some of the respect that Spanish society took away from Maricarmen.”
Visitors included some of the housing campaigners who had helped Maricarmen fight off previous eviction attempts. “This is really hard to take,” said Miguel, 59, fighting back tears as he added a red rose to the memorial. “When money is more powerful than people’s lives, it’s unbelievable.”
He said he hoped Maricarmen’s death would mark a turning point in Spain. “At least now we’re talking about this and putting names to those who are being evicted,” he said. “Because until now, there were 44 people a day being forced out of their homes. To the people in power, those are just numbers – now at least we’ve started putting names to those going through this.”
The Madrid tenants’ union announced a commemorative march at 8pm on Wednesday from the camp in the Puerta del Sol square to Abascal’s flat.
“Farewell, Maricarmen!” the union said in a post on social media . “Tonight we’ll honour you with a march … to the place that was your home for 70 years, and where you just wanted to stay until the end.”
Abascal’s ordeal has made housing a key issue in the forthcoming election, with Sánchez’s government seeking to push a redrafted package of measures through the council that operates when parliament has been dissolved. Meanwhile, the rightwing and far-right parties that opposed the legislation in congress last week have accused the prime minister of failing to act to address the housing crisis over the course of his eight years in office.
Sánchez offered his condolences to Abascal’s family and friends on Wednesday night. “A hug also to everyone who’s feeling this loss today as their own,” he wrote on social media. “Rest in peace.”
after newsletter promotion
Alberto Núñez Feijóo, the leader of the conservative People’s party (PP), which voted against last week’s emergency measures, also offered his condolences.
“No campaigning, no political parties, no partisan ends, no more bricks in the wall,” he wrote on social media. “When a person dies, there should be nothing but respect.”
The following day, however, Feijóo accused the government of trying to “manipulate the emotions of the Spanish people” by focusing on one particular eviction when there had been countless others during Sánchez’s time in office.
PP politicians also joined forces with the far right on Thursday to veto attempts to hold a minute’s silence for Maricarmen in Madrid’s regional parliament and the country’s senate. In Madrid’s municipal council, meanwhile, a rightwing attempt to block a minute’s silence was thwarted by opposition parties.
Abascal’s death has prompted reflection on how she had been treated by politicians and the media. The far-right Vox party, which also voted down the new decrees, had falsely suggested that Maricarmen would have had a home had she been an immigrant from North Africa , while one commentator had opined that “Maricarmen was chosen during a casting call for people facing eviction” to become a leftwing saint.
At least two far-right figures, including one of Vox’s MEPs, sought to sow doubt over the cause of Abascal’s death, with one even suggesting an autopsy should be carried out to determine whether the government had been involved . Another wrote : “Maricarmen was probably already made to send in her postal vote before they did her in. I expect anything from this scum.”

articles.title_orig: Google Cloud introduces Gemini agent for work as AI race heats up
articles.title_zh: Google Cloud introduces Gemini agent for work as AI race heats up
articles.content_orig:
Google on Thursday unveiled a new AI agent tailored for workplace tasks, positioning it to compete with other technology giants racing to offer their own virtual office assistants.
Called Gemini, the AI is a "universal agent" that can write and run code, create images and media and integrate with Google products like Gmail, Docs, Drive and Sheets, as well as third-party apps like Slack and Microsoft 365, Google said in its statement .
Thomas Kurian, the CEO of Google Cloud, shared the new product during a keynote address at Gemini at Work 2026 on Thursday, an annual event where Google showcases its suite of AI technology.
Google said the agent can seamlessly integrate into people's workflow, acting like a co-worker that can carry out tasks autonomously. Workers can delegate tasks to the agent, and it will return a finished product, Kurian said in the company's blog post.
"Gemini can function as your personal assistant or as a team member, where it works on behalf of a group of people, like a project manager within a team, or on behalf of a specific role in an organization, like an analyst in your finance department," he wrote.
To execute on certain tasks, Gemini can create its own "sub-agents," which Google described as "temporary, job-specific agents, each with their own identity," that can work together to accomplish goals over several days.
The AI agent, which runs in the Cloud, is designed to build memory and skills based on the tasks it's assigned and the questions users ask it.
"You never have to re-brief it or wonder which machine you told it to do something on," Kurian wrote in the blog post.
Gemini joins a growing field of AI agents marketed for personal and workplace use. In September, Meta introduced Muse , a personal AI assistant that has been downloaded millions of times. OpenAI followed suit late last month with the introduction of "Dots" , an "AI helper" available to ChatGPT users with Pro and Business Premium accounts.

articles.title_orig: USS Abraham Lincoln to dock in San Diego after harrowing stretch at sea
articles.title_zh: USS Abraham Lincoln to dock in San Diego after harrowing stretch at sea
articles.content_orig:
Deployment for nearly a year was marked by reports of supply shortages and deteriorating morale and mental health among crew
The USS Abraham Lincoln, the US aircraft carrier that has been deployed for nearly a year and has spent months supporting US military operations against Iran, is scheduled to dock in San Diego on Thursday afternoon.
It marks the end of a deployment that has been described as “one of the most operationally intense and consequential of the modern era” and that became marked by a record-setting stretch at sea, repeated deployment extensions, and reports of supply shortages and deteriorating morale and mental health among some crew members.
The Lincoln left San Diego last November, initially bound for the Pacific. But it was redirected to the Middle East after the US and Israel launched their war with Iran in late February. The carrier remained there until late August, when it was relieved by the USS George Washington and began its journey home .
Earlier in August, the Lincoln’s deployment made headlines and faced scrutiny as reports began surfacing about poor living conditions onboard the ship, including shortages of supplies and water, plumbing problems, low morale and worsening mental health among the roughly 5,000 personnel on the carrier. Two leading military newspapers also reported that there had been two attempts by sailors to jump overboard, causing concern among families and military health experts.
The reports prompted outrage from Democrats , while senior officials in the Trump administration pushed back . Pete Hegseth, the US defense secretary, called the reports “completely misrepresented ”, and when reporters asked Donald Trump if he thought the deployment had gone on too long, he responded : “Not nearly long enough” – a comment that angered some naval families.
In a statement at the time, Adm Brad Cooper, who heads US Central Command, claimed that of the US navy’s 11 active aircraft carriers, the Lincoln had “among the lowest number of cases related to mental health”. But he said that “this doesn’t mean that all is perfect”.
Cooper said that a long deployment at sea “is uniquely challenging and tough, and every single one of us, including me, reacts to stressors in different ways”.
Two weeks ago, as the Lincoln headed back to San Diego, Hung Cao, the acting navy secretary, acknowledged that eight service members from the Lincoln and its accompanying strike group attempted to take their own lives.
Sara Jacobs, a Democrat representing California’s 51st district who visited the Lincoln in late September, said in a statement last week that while she is “relieved that the USS Abraham Lincoln will soon be back in San Diego” and “looking forward to welcoming them home”, her “demand for accountability won’t end when they make port”.
“I will continue pushing for an [office of the inspector general] investigation into these conditions and a House armed services committee field hearing in San Diego to hear directly from these service members,” she said. “We need to prevent this crisis from happening ever again, and ultimately end the Iran war and bring all our service members home.”
On Wednesday, Hegseth visited the Lincoln ahead of its return, and praised the crew. He acknowledged that their deployment had not been “easy”.
“When you greet your families tomorrow, just pass my gratitude from the president and myself,” Hegseth said. “Let them know that their long wait, we believe, was in service of a righteous and historic mission.”
During his remarks, Hegseth announced that those onboard the vessel would be awarded the presidential unit citation, which, according to the US military , is conferred on units of the armed forces “for extraordinary heroism in action against an armed enemy”.
Ahead of the Lincoln’s arrival on Thursday afternoon, Blue Star Families, one of the largest US-based non-profit organizations supporting active military service members, veterans and their families, said in a statement that “every homecoming is an important moment for military families”.
The organization said that it “welcomes home the sailors of USS Abraham Lincoln and wants every family to know they’re not alone as they reconnect”.
In the weeks ahead, Blue Star Families said it will host appreciation days for Lincoln sailors and their families, including several events next month in San Diego.

articles.title_orig: Third Life World Signs Definitive Agreement to Acquire Transglobal Management Group, Inc.
articles.title_zh: Third Life World Signs Definitive Agreement to Acquire Transglobal Management Group, Inc.
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
Persistent AI-agent world on Base to become the operating business of the public company
LAS VEGAS, Oct. 08, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Third Life World, LLC ("Third Life World"), the developer of a persistent online world where AI agents own land, build, work and trade, today announced that it has signed a definitive Control Share Purchase Agreement with Transglobal Management Group, Inc. (OTC: TMGI) ("TMGI" or the "Company") and its controlling shareholder, Marc Angell.
Under the agreement, Third Life World acquires the voting control of the Company which expects to make Third Life World's platform its core operating business.
Third Life World acquires the Series A Preferred control block which holds a majority of the voting rights.
TMGI will create a new Series B Preferred Stock to assist with this purchase.
At closing, Marc Angell will step down from his officer positions at TMGI. He will remain available to the Company as a consultant to support a smooth transition.
New management and board designees will be named by Third Life World in accordance with applicable notice and filing requirements.
Closing is subject to customary conditions, including transfer-agent processing and the filing of the Series B Certificate of Designation with the Florida Secretary of State.
About the Third Life World platform
Third Life World ( thirdlifeworld.xyz ) is a live, persistent world built on the Base blockchain. Players create AI agents that claim land, construct buildings, gather resources, earn ranks and trade on an in-world marketplace, with activity settled in the platform's native currency, $AMETA. The world runs continuously on a timed "tick" cycle, so agents keep working and the economy keeps moving even when their owners are offline.
As of September 14, 2026, the platform reported 4,780 players , 5,004 AI agents and 2,111 of 5,625 land parcels claimed , with 25 building types available. The platform earns revenue through a 1% fee on in-world transactions, agent creation, premium agent subscriptions and land and building sales. It also offers an API that lets outside developers connect their own AI agents to the world.
Growth plan Over the next six months, the Company plans to:
Launch Version 3 of the world, adding map visibility, NPC movement, vehicles and deeper customization;
Release mobile apps on the Apple App Store and Google Play;
Publish public API documentation and onboard outside developers and partners; and
Grow toward its target of 50,000 users.
Management commentary "Taking control of a public company gives Third Life World a platform to scale," said Jorge Guinovart, Managing Member of Third Life World, LLC. "We've built a live world where AI agents already own land, build and trade around the clock. With TMGI, we can bring that to a much larger audience, fund mobile and Version 3, and give our community a transparent public company to follow."
"We are pleased to hand TMGI to a team with a live product and a clear plan, and I look forward to supporting the transition." said Marc Angell, outgoing CEO of TMGI.
About Transglobal Management Group, Inc. Transglobal Management Group, Inc. (OTCID: TMGI) is a publicly traded company listed on the OTC Markets Basic platform, headquartered in St. Petersburg, Florida.
About Third Life World, LLC Third Life World, LLC is a Nevada limited liability company based in Las Vegas. It builds and operates Third Life World, a persistent AI-agent world and economy on the Base blockchain. Learn more at thirdlifeworld.xyz and on X at @ThirdLifeWorld .
Media and investor contact For Third Life World, LLC: Jorge Guinovart 723 South 7th Street, Las Vegas, Nevada 89101 jorgeguini@gmail.com
For TMGI: Marc Angell marc@tmgiusa.com

articles.title_orig: ‘The Floating World’ by Ben Eastham, Reviewed
articles.title_zh: ‘The Floating World’ by Ben Eastham, Reviewed
articles.content_orig:
For all its suspicion of the contemporary artworld and its machinations, the art critic’s debut novel remains surprisingly sincere about art itself
The unnamed narrator of Ben Eastham’s debut novel, The Floating World , is, like Eastham himself , an art critic. Grieving his recently deceased wife, he feels lost while teaching at a school where the students refer to him as ‘Doctor Pissington’. Then a friend offers him a job back in the artworld. He is to work on ‘The Floating World’, which is ‘a gated community beneath a giant dome on a desert island’ being built by a tech billionaire for the wealthiest as a refuge from climate crisis and political collapse. Our morally conflicted protagonist is hired to conduct research for an art exhibition marking the island’s inauguration. The novel negotiates the contradiction of inhabiting a contemporary artworld sustained by the good intentions of art workers who align themselves with beauty and virtue, while depending on the very forces their work purports to resist.
It opens with the narrator, in Ireland, on the verge of writing, before disappearing into his recollections, and eventually returns to the point at which the story is being written (more on which later). Grief provides its emotional landscape: the narrator’s reality is shot through with the frenetic despair that comes with the sudden loss of his wife. His grief gradually becomes entangled with the project of ‘The Floating World’ and the people making it, forcing a confrontation with the loss he has been carrying. It is in such experiences that resist ordinary expression that art becomes most meaningful: a painting, for example, that is ‘a truth that didn’t need explaining. No aristocrats, no symbolism, no lies. A painting clear as love’; and another, when the narrator’s friend likens the experience of pregnancy to a painting they once saw in a museum, in which ‘The colours are stronger and brighter, there’s a texture. It’s like breaking through a screen, the world feels bigger, like it can’t be contained.’
Eastham is at his most sensitive when criticism itself becomes inadequate. There is a pleasing irony in an art critic writing about an art critic for whom, and for the artists around him, the most profound encounters with art seem to occur precisely when interpretation fails. While Eastham is tender in his descriptions of art, his acute observations of the people surrounding it can be lacerating. He has a formidable talent for summoning up a character – or skewering one – in a sentence. One woman possesses ‘the erotic hauteur of an academic who in her youth danced beneath filtered spotlights at psychedelic happenings’. Another, ‘a woman in those oversized metal-rimmed spectacles designed to signal to civilians that the wearer is an intellectual’. Eastham is exacting not only when it comes to how people appear, but also about the identities they are trying, sometimes desperately, to project. Despite the grieving anguish of its narrator, it is his wry, deadpan humour that carries the novel. There is a dryly comic sparring match with a ‘philanthropist’ who believes happiness can be quantified, and a conversation between partygoers about where, literally, ‘the shit is going’. At times it is not unlike a drawing-room comedy, with its sharp wit, back-and-forth banter and clever insults.
The metafictional frame allows the novel to avoid the aftermath of its most dramatic events, dwelling instead on the act of remembering and reconstructing them. I’m not convinced this framing adds to the reader’s understanding of the narrator’s grief or the events being recounted. The narrator returns to remarkably similar emotional terrain at the end: melancholic and still lost, but perhaps slightly more hopeful for the future. For all its suspicion of the contemporary artworld and its machinations, The Floating World remains surprisingly sincere about art itself. This is especially persuasive when Eastham uses art to give shape to experiences that elude explanation – love, pregnancy, grief – reminding us that beneath the bullshit posturing of the artworld is an unexpectedly earnest faith that art can make felt what we cannot quite articulate.
The Floating World by Ben Eastham. Fitzcarraldo Editions , £14.99 (softcover)

The International Lineman's Rodeo Week brings together lineworkers and their families from around the world. Started in 1984, the event celebrates the line trade with the Safety and Training Conference, Lineman's Expo, Trade Night and BBQ, annual competition and awards banquet.
For 2026, the event will take place from Oct. 14-17 in Kansas City, with the conference, trade show, Trade Night and awards banquet at the Overland Park Convention Center and the competition at the Agricultural Hall of Fame grounds in Bonner Springs, Kansas.
If you have a photo, video or story that you want to share with us from the 2026 International Lineman's Rodeo Week, please share it with Amy Fischbach , Head of Content for T&D World and host of the Line Life Podcast.

articles.title_orig: Odyssey Launches Odyssey-3, Its Most Powerful Foundation World Model Built to Power AI Across the Physical World
articles.title_zh: Odyssey Launches Odyssey-3, Its Most Powerful Foundation World Model Built to Power AI Across the Physical World
articles.content_orig:
Odyssey Launches Odyssey-3, Its Most Powerful Foundation World Model Built to Power AI Across the Physical World
New model demonstrates a shared understanding of the world across robots, humanoids, vehicles, drones, AI agents, and video games
Odyssey , an AI research company pioneering foundation world models, today announced Odyssey-3, its most powerful world model to date. The new model represents a significant advance toward general-purpose intelligence that can understand, predict, and interact with both physical and virtual environments.
This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261008756684/en/
Caption: Odyssey’s latest world model powering Flexion’s robot. Credit: Odyssey
World models learn from vast examples of the world evolving to predict and simulate what happens next, including how actions affect outcomes. Odyssey-3 gives intelligent systems a general understanding of how the world works before they are taught a specific task. The model has shown the ability to control robots and humanoids, drive vehicles, pilot drones, generate environments for training AI agents, and play video games. The new model has already been adopted by companies including Flexion, a leader in humanoid autonomy.
Trained on a vast dataset of visual observations of the world, Odyssey-3 builds on world models the company has been developing over the past three years. It has learned representations of physics, dynamics, cause and effect, and human behavior that can be applied across physical and virtual systems.
Using this pretrained foundation, Odyssey-3 enables physical agents: intelligent systems that can apply a shared understanding of the world across different machines, environments, and tasks. Rather than learning every new task entirely from scratch, these systems can draw on a broader model of how the world works and adapt that knowledge to new situations with relatively little additional experience.
“Odyssey-3 is a big step toward a single intelligence that can understand and operate in the world around us,” said Oliver Cameron, co-founder and CEO of Odyssey . “World models give physical agents a foundation of knowledge they can carry from one machine, environment, or task to another. We believe that the ability to learn broadly and then adapt with relatively little experience is the path toward increasingly general physical intelligence.”
The company has demonstrated Odyssey-3 across six domains:
Odyssey-3 is designed as a foundation that can span these domains rather than a model optimized for a single machine or application. By learning common representations of how environments behave and how actions change them, Odyssey is working toward world models that can transfer knowledge across increasingly diverse physical and virtual systems.
Odyssey is an AI lab pioneering general world models: causal, multimodal systems that learn to predict and interact with the world over long horizons. This foundational technology promises to revolutionize robotics, science, healthcare, education, gaming, defense, and beyond.
Odyssey’s founders previously pioneered one of the most complex applications of physical AI: self-driving cars. They’ve since brought together a world-class research team from DeepMind, Tesla, Waymo, Meta, Apple, and Wayve, whose members have contributed to language models, video models, world models and autonomous systems, including DeepMind Gemini, DeepMind Veo, Wayve GAIA and Tesla FSD.
Media: media@odyssey.systems

articles.title_orig: World Sight Day: Restoring sight where cataract surgery is scarce
articles.title_zh: World Sight Day: Restoring sight where cataract surgery is scarce
articles.content_orig:
Lloyd Williams, MD, PhD, discusses rising cataract blindness and low-cost surgery in conflict zones for World Sight Day.
Cataract remains a leading cause of vision impairment and blindness worldwide. At least 2.2 billion people have a near or distance vision impairment, and in at least 1 billion of those cases, the impairment could have been prevented or has yet to be addressed, according to the World Health Organization (WHO). Cataract accounts for 94 million of those cases, and 1 in 2 people who need cataract surgery do not have access to it.¹
World Sight Day is an annual day of awareness held on the second Thursday of October and coordinated by the International Agency for the Prevention of Blindness (IAPB). This year, it falls on October 8. The 2026 #LoveYourEyes campaign centers on personal stories, lived experiences, and community action ahead of the first Global Summit for Eye Health on November 2 in Antigua and Barbuda.²
To mark the occasion, Lloyd Williams, MD, PhD , director of Duke Global Ophthalmology at Duke Eye Center in Durham, North Carolina, spoke with Ophthalmology Times about why cataract blindness continues to rise and how teams deliver high-quality surgery in low-resource settings. Williams received the American Academy of Ophthalmology's 2025 Outstanding Humanitarian Service Award for expanding access to cataract and corneal surgery in underserved regions.
Williams attributed the increase to aging populations in regions where ophthalmic care has not expanded, compounded by conflict and poverty that make many areas harder to reach. He cited a recent cataract camp in South Sudan.
"We literally had to negotiate a ceasefire in order to do cataract surgery," Williams told Ophthalmology Times .
Williams highlighted several organizations working to expand access to eye care. Readers can donate or get involved through the following: • Duke Global Ophthalmology: Give to Duke GO .³ • Cure Blindness Project: Donate ; ophthalmologists and practices can also join its Global Partners Program.⁴ • IAPB: Individuals can become a Love Your Eyes Visionary , and organizations can apply for membership .⁵ • CBM (Christian Blind Mission): Donate .⁶ • Sightsavers: Donate or fundraise through Sightsavers USA.⁷
On a recent trip to Abyei, surgery cost approximately $70 per case using manual small incision cataract surgery (MSICS), which requires a microscope as the only electrical equipment. In skilled hands, Williams said, MSICS achieves results roughly equivalent to those in the US. A $700,000 donation this year is expected to fund approximately 9000 surgeries, a volume he said would not be possible with phacoemulsification or laser-based approaches.
"I strongly believe that we're not providing somebody substandard care," Williams said.
Williams also addressed studies linking cataract surgery to lower rates of dementia diagnosis, which cannot yet establish cause and effect. He recalled veterans whose anxiety and depression appeared to improve after surgery during his residency, and he said he discusses the cognitive benefits of sight with families of older patients. Reflecting on his own vision problem as a resident, he described sight as "something that you could lose just like your arm."

articles.title_orig: Arizona congressional candidate says she was raped while repairing campaign sign
articles.title_zh: Arizona congressional candidate says she was raped while repairing campaign sign
articles.content_orig:
A congressional candidate in Arizona has said she was raped in a car park as she repaired campaign signs late at night in her district.
Bernadette Greene-Placentia, a Democrat, told the Phoenix New Times she was knocked unconscious during the alleged attack in the Phoenix suburb of Sun City on 14 August, waking up to find a man on top of her.
She said she did not initially notify police until filing a report with the Maricopa County Sheriff's Office two weeks later.
Her Republican opponent, Abraham Hamadeh, urged authorities in a statement to "investigate these serious allegations thoroughly, including finding all possible camera footage of the time and place".
"No American should become a victim of a crime in their own community," said Hamadeh, who is running for a second term in office.
Greene-Placentia told the Phoenix New Times she was "embarrassed" and "just wanted to forget", but felt compelled stand up for other victims.
The candidate said she often speaks on the campaign trail about fighting for Arizonans.
She told the Phoenix New Times: "I didn't feel like I could keep saying that if I weren't also fighting for women that are victims of sexual assault."
The BBC has contacted the Maricopa County Sheriff's Office for comment. A sheriff's spokesman told the New York Times the investigation was ongoing.
After the attack, Greene-Placentia said she withdrew from the public for two days, staying in an apartment separate from her husband and skipping a campaign event.
When she emerged, her husband, campaign staff and others in her circle noticed she was acting differently, according to Phoenix New Times.
Greene-Placentia said she did not see a doctor following the alleged attack in congressional district eight and did not receive a sexual assault examination.
She said her memory of what happened was spotty and she did not get a good look at either of the two assailants, but described them as white men, according to the New York Times.
She told the Phoenix New Times that one assailant may have made a comment about her political affiliation, together with a misogynistic slur, although she could not be certain.
The candidate said she was concerned voters might think it was a political stunt to win points in a heavily Republican district. She also expressed concern that the allegations might overshadow her messaging around affordability.

articles.title_orig: Webinar will commemorate World Food Day with theme “Innovate today. Nourish tomorrow”
articles.title_zh: Webinar will commemorate World Food Day with theme “Innovate today. Nourish tomorrow”
articles.content_orig:
A webinar on 16 October will commemorate World Food Day and say farewell to the UN special rapporteur for the Right to Water and Sanitation.
The webinar will take the World Food Day theme “ Innovate today. Nourish tomorrow.” The discussion will explore what innovation can look like when we place food security, water, land, human rights, and ecological sustainability at the centre.
World Food Day is observed on 16 October each year and provides an opportunity to draw attention to hunger and food insecurity while strengthening collective action towards food systems that are sustainable, equitable, and resilient. This year ’ s webinar will bring together United Nations mandate holders, faith-based organisations, civil society organisations, and community practitioners to explore some of the challenges shaping food insecurity today – including poverty, unsustainable agricultural practices and climate change – and to share approaches that are contributing to resilience, food sovereignty, and sustainable livelihoods.
The session will also provide an opportunity to hear from Prof. Pedro Arrojo-Agudo, UN special rapporteur on the human right to safe drinking water and sanitation, whose six-year mandate concludes in November 2026.

articles.title_orig: Old World Industries and Integrity Systems Form Strategic Partnership to Bring Real-Time Coolant Intelligence to AI Data Centers
articles.title_zh: Old World Industries and Integrity Systems Form Strategic Partnership to Bring Real-Time Coolant Intelligence to AI Data Centers
articles.content_orig:
NORTHBROOK, Ill. and WEATHERFORD, Texas, Oct. 8, 2026
Thermal Charge® Heat Transfer Fluids and AI-Powered Monitoring Unite to Deliver Predictive Cooling-Loop Health Management
NORTHBROOK, Ill. and WEATHERFORD, Texas , Oct. 8, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Old World Industries (OWI), a leading manufacturer of coolant and heat transfer solutions best known for its brands of PEAK® and Thermal Charge® Heat Transfer Fluids, and Integrity Systems, a critical infrastructure monitoring company, today announced a strategic partnership to combine coolant expertise with real-time monitoring, predictive analytics and intelligent diagnostics for data center cooling systems.
As AI and other high-density computing workloads place increasing demands on data center infrastructure, operators need greater visibility into the real-time health and performance of their cooling systems. Any downtime or disruptions to the system can have significant operational and financial consequences, making proactive monitoring and maintenance critical for data center operators. Periodic laboratory testing provides important point-in-time information about coolant condition; the OWI-Integrity Systems partnership is designed to complement that testing with continuous field monitoring that can alert operators of changing cooling-loop conditions between testing intervals.
"Unscheduled downtime remains one of the most expensive risks facing data center operators today," said Greg Noethlich, Chief Executive Officer of OWI. "This partnership helps customers move from reactive problem-solving to predictive maintenance, helping avoid the substantial costs associated with unexpected system failures."
Integrity Systems' real-time industrial monitoring, predictive analytics and intelligent diagnostics capabilities are designed to work alongside existing controls and monitoring systems. Its platform brings together sensor data, operating context, maintenance history and operator knowledge to help identify developing problems and guide maintenance decisions.
"We founded Integrity Systems to close the gap between what industrial operators need and what predictive monitoring actually delivers," said Brett Wade, Chief Executive Officer of Integrity Systems. "By combining continuous field monitoring with OWI's coolant expertise, the partnership delivers ongoing visibility into coolant performance, helping operators make informed maintenance decisions based on real-time operating conditions."
The collaboration also creates an opportunity to generate additional real-world operating data on coolant performance. Those insights can help inform future product validation and development while giving operators greater context about cooling system conditions in live environments.
"We see AI's future being shaped not only by the size of the data centers behind it, but by the ability to deploy increasing levels of intelligence at the edge," said Connor Wooley, Chief Technology Officer of Integrity Systems. "Our goal is to lead in that space by delivering AI where work is performed and critical decisions are made. Our agentic harness is designed to turn deep analysis and verified operating experience into specialized AI that runs locally. With OWI, we're applying that approach to coolant and cooling-system health, helping operators understand what is changing, why it matters, and when to act. But our vision extends further, an operating system for intelligent infrastructure that can carry that capability beyond continuous human reach, from remote industrial environments to space. The goal is intelligence that can operate where people cannot always be, without depending on a distant data center for every decision."
Together, OWI and Integrity Systems are enabling a new standard for cooling-system assurance that helps data center operators improve uptime, protect critical infrastructure and confidently scale for growing computing demands. To learn more about the partnership, visit thermalcharge.com or integrityus.ai.

articles.title_orig: New GETI publication explores future of Christian unity
articles.title_zh: New GETI publication explores future of Christian unity
articles.content_orig:
A new publication from the World Council of Churches (WCC) Commission on Ecumenical Education and Formation (EEF) brings together the voices and theological reflections of young ecumenists from around the world who attended the 2025 edition of the WCC Global Ecumenical Theological Institute (GETI). It brings fresh inputs to the pressing question for the churches today: Where now for visible unity?
From left: Rev. Prof. Dr Meehyun Chung, moderator of the WCC Commission on Ecumenical Education and Formation; Prof. Dr Ani Ghazaryan Drissi, WCC programme executive for Ecumenical Theological Education and coordinator of GETI 2025; Rev. Dr Nathan Digby, GETI 2025 facilitator and member of the WCC Commission on Ecumenical Education and Formation; during the launch event of the GETI 2025 book on 8 October.
“ GETI 2025: Voices and Visions of Transformative Unity,” edited by Prof. Dr Ani Ghazaryan Drissi and Rev. Prof. Teddy Chalwe Sakupapa, emerges from the WCC ’ s 4th GETI, held in the context of the Sixth World Conference on Faith and Order in Wadi El Natrun, Egypt. The publication, launched on 8 October, during the biannual meeting of the EEF Commission, comes at a significant moment.
“ The fruits of ecumenical dialogue must take root in the lives of our churches,” said Ghazaryan. “ The GETI 2025 message brought this bold challenge to the Sixth World Conference on Faith and Order and the wider ecumenical movement: let the unity we confess become the life we share.”
This publication carries that call forward, she added, through voices and visions rooted in different churches, cultures, and lived realities. “ Their theological reflections invite us to ask how the fruits of ecumenical dialogue can shape our communities, deepen our relationships, and renew our common witness,” said Ghazaryan. “ They call us to listen more deeply, confront exclusion, and share responsibility for the future of our churches.”
Bossey students who took part of GETI 2025 shared their testimonies during the launch event.
The volume presents a global and contextually grounded exploration of Christian unity. Its contributors reflect on reception, Nicaea, pilgrimage, trust and companionship, while also addressing colonial wounds, trauma, migration, ethnic violence, Palestine, digital ecumenism, and ecological crisis.
Rather than treating unity as an abstract theological ideal, the book emphasizes unity as something that must be embodied through relationships, truth-telling, healing, solidarity, and public witness. Its concluding message describes young ecumenists as contributors to the present and future of the ecumenical movement.
GETI 2025 facilitator and EEF commissioner Rev. Dr Nathan Digby explained that a central goal of the WCC ’ s Ecumenical Theological Education work is to provide opportunities for emerging ecumenical leaders to be formed in ecumenism and to ensure that their voices are heard, encouraged, and shared with the wider church.
“ The publication of GETI 2025: Voices and Visions for Transformative Unity gives concrete expression to this commitment,” he said. “ As part of their theological formation, students participating in GETI 2025 developed academic papers exploring the theme of visible Christian unity in relation to their own theological interests, contexts, and experiences.”
This volume recognizes and celebrates their intellectual and theological work while creating a platform through which their perspectives can contribute to broader conversations about the future of Christian unity, added Digby.
“ By bringing these emerging voices together in one publication, GETI 2025: Voices and Visions for Transformative Unity not only documents an important dimension of the GETI experience but also invests in the next generation of ecumenical thinkers and leaders, whose insights and visions are essential for shaping a more transformative and visible unity among Christians.”
Published by WCC Publications, the book offers churches, theological institutions, students, and ecumenical partners a rich resource for reflection and conversation on the future of Christian unity.
The session also included the presentation of the GETI Visual Report and a short video featuring voices and moments of GETI 2025.
The EEF Commission is meeting at the WCC Ecumenical Institute at Bossey 4-9 October.

Imagine the sun has just risen as you wake to the soft sounds of Martian dust swirling outside. You look out and what do you see? A beautiful mountain range, bathed in golden light.
While this imaginary scenario might not be possible today, if future astronauts ever get to enjoy their morning coffee on the Red Planet, this is what they might see.
NASA's Curiosity rover recently captured a stunning new panorama of dawn breaking over a Mars mountain range
The panorama , made using six different shots captured of the view, showcases Martian cliffs on the northwestern edge of Mount Sharp.
Curiosity has been exploring this 3-mile-tall (5-kilometer-tall) mountain for over a decade. Crawling up the mountain since 2014, the rover has explored all sorts of strange and unusual terrain. And now? It has captured a beautiful, peaceful Martian morning.
Looking at this image, it seems almost Earth-like. Despite the complete lack of plant life (or any life that we're aware of), the view is reminiscent of mountains rising out of the deserts on our very own planet.
But what might feel like a familiar sight in a national park is an entirely different planet.
And by enjoying this view (and analyzing it scientifically), researchers can better understand how features like the cliffs on Mount Sharp formed.
Mars was once home to a variety of bodies of water like lakes and rivers. But what happened to the planet once it lost its atmosphere and, subsequently, its liquid surface water? How did the minerals left behind from these streams and lakes affect the Martian topography? These are just some of the many questions researchers aim to answer with observations like this.

With a M.S. in Biology, Chelsea has written and worked for institutions including NASA JPL, the American Museum of Natural History, Scientific American, Discover Magazine Blog, Astronomy Magazine, and Live Science. When not writing, editing or filming something space-y, Gohd is writing music and performing as Foxanne, even launching a song to space in 2021 with Inspiration4. articles.title_orig: Amoris laetitia: Pastoral experiences in Asia and challenges of digital world
articles.title_zh: Amoris laetitia: Pastoral experiences in Asia and challenges of digital world
articles.content_orig:
Families today are âa challenging mosaic of diverse realities, marked by joys, hopes, struggles and wounds. The family is not only a place to which the Church brings the Gospel. It is also a place from which the Gospel comes alive â from one generation to another, from one family to another, and from families to society.â
Cardinal Filipe Neri Ferrão, Metropolitan Archbishop of Goa and Daman, opened his address with this reflection at the start of the second day of Pope Leo XIVâs meeting with the heads of the Eastern Churches and the presidents of the Bishopsâ Conferences, ten years after Amoris laetitia .
The Indian Cardinal addressed the theme âFamilies today: reality, beauty and challenges. Discerning the signs of the times through the experience of families and the Churchâs pastoral commitment today.â
He invited participants in the meeting, conducted in a synodal style, to ask themselves in their discernment: âWhat is the Holy Spirit asking the Church to change?â
This concerned ânot only in what we do for the families, but in how we understand, accompany and empower them as protagonists of the Gospel and as enduring loci of Godâs revelation.â
Drawing on his experience as a pastor in Asia, particularly in India, Cardinal Neri Ferrão acknowledged that families had changed in their identity, nature, and composition, with smaller households, new forms of cohabitation, and interreligious marriages.
Families were increasingly on the move, and many faced economic insecurity, poverty, unemployment, and uncertainty about the future.
âChristian families in many parts of India and Asia,â the Cardinal stressed, âmust also live amid growing religious polarisation and hostility, making the public expression and transmission of faith increasingly difficult.â
Yet, these families also offered the Church beauty through their care for children, the elderly, the sick, and vulnerable people. Even amid poverty and uncertainty, the Cardinal explained, âour families continue to create positive spaces for joy and hope.â
Following the publication of Amoris laetitia , he recalled, the Churches in India and across Asia âlistened first to families,â and that listening âshaped how we walk with them. We now see marriage preparation as the start of a lifelong journey, offer spiritual renewal and counselling to couples and children, and keep forming families and lay leaders over time.â
He stressed that pastoral ministry needed to move âfrom mission to families to mission among families.â Families were not simply recipients of assistance but, in his words, âthe Church's partners in mission.â
Cardinal Neri Ferrão concluded by recounting the experience of a priest who had begun family ministry in his parish not with a program, but by visiting a family experiencing underlying difficulties in communication between the parents and between them and their children. It had begun with âa conversation and a willingness to listen.â
The second speaker, Vincenzo Rosito, Professor of the History and Culture of Family Institutions at the Pontifical Lateran University and Vice Dean of the Pontifical John Paul II Theological Institute for Marriage and Family Sciences, summed up his address with questions to guide participantsâ synodal discernment.
He began with an invitation inspired by Pope Leo XIVâs reflections in the encyclical Magnifica humanitas : âLet each of us be mindful of the relationships we build within our own families and within the Church.â
Professor Rosito stressed that âfamily practices, in fact, help us to understand how churches and families learn from one another. Both the Church and the family, in fact, learn through the practices of their daily lives.â
He then offered a question for participants to consider as a father, mother, theologian, or pastor: âAm I able to recognise and share with others at least one new thing that I have learnt to do, or to do differently, in recent years of my family or pastoral life?â
Changes in family life, Prof. Rosito explained, âare not problemsâ but âhuman activities.â Recalling Amoris laetitia , he presented them as an opportunity, as concrete processes âin which individuals and families act, react, learn and develop new resources.â
âConsider, for example,â the political philosopher continued, âhow the use of new digital technologies is transforming the daily habits of families and the way children are brought up.â
The family and the Church, Prof. Rosito continued, âlearn together through change.â He drew on the Gospel image of Jesus, Joseph, and Maryâs flight into Egypt.
He noted that today, âdrawing on the experiences of refugee and migrant families, some Christian communities are re-establishing themselves as ârefuge churchesââ for those arriving in a new land or making a long journey.
He also addressed the tragedy of violence shared by many families: âThe insecurity stemming from social and political violence is a worrying reality that many Churches must deal with today, in their daily lives.â Such insecurity, he warned, could âeven devour family bonds and church relationships themselves.â
Josephâs dream was also part of the experience of this flight.
âTo dream, to imagine new forms for the Church,â Prof. Rosito concluded, âalso means renewing what we already do. To imagine the Church means being willing to learn from one another, whilst we are transformed together, as churches and as families.â
His final question for discernment was therefore: âWhat do we need, amidst the light and shadow of today, to learn and imagine new ways of being a family and new ways of being the Church?â

articles.title_orig: Italy approves elections overhaul as opposition accuse Meloni of 'scam' law
articles.title_zh: Italy approves elections overhaul as opposition accuse Meloni of 'scam' law
articles.content_orig:
Italy's parliament has approved fiercely contested changes to the country's electoral system championed by Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni ahead of elections due next year.
Lawmakers voted 227 to 164 in favour of moving to a fully proportional system, which Meloni has argued will boost the chance of clear winners and more stable government.
Opposition parties say her right-wing coalition has designed the proposals to improve its chance of retaining power and, in a heated debate on Thursday, accused it of pushing through the "fraudulent" reform to flout democracy.
Meloni had warned she could resign and trigger an early election if the plans were rejected, with the secret ballot seen as a test of her authority.
Meloni's coalition has overseen a rare period of political stability for Italy since her election in 2022, and last month her government became the country's longest-running since World War Two.
The voting reform will see the country move away from its current hybrid voting system, in which about a third of members are chosen through a first-past-the-post vote and the rest through proportional representation.
Parties proposing to form a coalition will be required to put forward their joint candidate for prime minister, and their political programme, before any general election.
A party or coalition which emerges with the largest share of the votes - provided this exceeds 42% - will be awarded 105 additional seats in parliament (70 in the lower house and 35 in the senate), which could turn a narrow victory into a more comfortable majority.
Centre-left members held up signs with slogans including "No to the scam" and "fraudulent law" during a debate ahead of the vote, and accused the government of forcing through the new voting rules.
"Go ahead and change the electoral law, we will win in any case under any voting system," said Democratic Party (PD) leader Elly Schlein.
Five Star leader and former Prime Minister Giuseppe Conte told AFP news agency that the move was "a mess, a convoluted scheme, devised solely to find a formula to gain an advantage in the upcoming elections".
The proposals have also exposed tensions within the ranks of Meloni's coalition, too, with the Brothers of Italy (FdI) party and its allies, the far-right League and centre-right Forza Italia.
Analysts had predicted that Thursday's final vote was unlikely to fail - particularly given the number of lawmakers who would risk losing their eligibility for a parliamentary pension if their term was ended early as a result of the threatened snap election.
"To those who hoped to see the centre-right divided," Meloni wrote on social media after the vote, "today we respond with facts: we are united, cohesive, and determined to carry forward the commitments made to citizens."
She added: "We are introducing rules designed to promote the stability and parliamentary coherence of any government, regardless of its political colour."
Meloni's term officially comes to an end in October 2027, although she could bring elections forward to the spring.

articles.title_orig: Hundreds of new pro sports team ETFs lead world of retail investing to the edge of gambling
articles.title_zh: Hundreds of new pro sports team ETFs lead world of retail investing to the edge of gambling
articles.content_orig:
In 1989, all-time hits leader Pete Rose was banned from Major League Baseball for life because of his gambling activities. He wasn't reinstated until last year, months after his death in 2024.
Fast-forward to today, and Pete Rose's gambling might seem like just another day on Wall Street as financial firms expand the ways fans can put money behind their teams, beyond a beer and a $15 hot dog.
You may soon be able to buy a ticker for your favorite hockey team, and it isn't a stake in the franchise. Multiple asset managers have filed to launch dozens of ETFs, one for every NHL team, with MLB baseball team funds filed as well, all built on new futures contracts that track a team's season statistics. None has begun trading but in all, hundreds of ETFs that track the single-season performance of one professional team across a mix of statistical categories have been filed at the SEC for approval.
Some finance experts see the development as lacking any nuance whatsoever.
"The line between gambling and investing has not simply been blurred, it has been erased," said Robert Johnson, a professor of finance at Creighton University.
Among fund companies getting in on the novel trend are VolatilityShares , LeagueShares, Roundhill Investments , and Rex Financial .
None of the four companies responded to requests for comment. Asset managers typically cannot publicly comment during the period between when funds are filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission for approval and when they become effective, if approved.
Rex, a Miami-based ETF issuer, announced Sept. 21 that it was launching Alpha Sports Holdings, a new subsidiary built to turn team performance into exchange-traded funds. REX has filed with the SEC for BaseballShares and HockeyShares, suites of ETFs that would track Major League Baseball and National Hockey League teams through futures contracts that CME Group, the derivatives exchange, lists on indexes built by FutureSports, an index company. The underlying CME futures , which began trading for NHL teams in late September, need to first establish a trading history.
Each team's index opens the season at a set number and moves as the team racks up statistics, including runs scored, stolen bases and strikeouts for baseball, then resets in the offseason.
"The sports industry generates hundreds of billions of dollars a year, but there has never been a liquid, transparent investment product tied directly to what happens in live games," said Greg King, CEO of Alpha Sports, in a press release. "Alpha Sports exists to build that product for passionate investors who want to participate in the fortunes of their favorite teams."
Johnson, though, said the sports-themed ETFs are far more gaming than investing.
"I thought that the ETF world had jumped the shark with the introduction of the 2X and 3X leveraged and inverse ETFs. In my mind these were simply vehicles for short term speculators. But, at least these vehicles were based upon assets. The new structures — and I call them structures, not assets — are simply gambling dressed up as investing," Johnson said.
In fact, the proposed team ETFs include in some cases leveraged versions of trades on single-team performance.
The boom in prediction markets is already blurring the lines between sports wagering and market trading, with regulatory battles intensifying over the distinction — CNBC reported on Thursday that the NFL is pushing for prediction markets to be regulated by state gambling authorities. Unlike prediction markets contracts, the sports team ETFs are tracking futures off an index rather than a single event (e.g. win or loss). But while structurally contracts in this market have a role to play for investors, in the case of sports performance, Johnson says the case is weak.
"They have societal value in that parties are able to hedge natural positions and transact with other speculators willing to bear that risk. This allows a more optimal allocation of risk," Johnson said.
But he added that is not the case when individual investors are making bets on the performance of sports teams they follow.
"There are no natural positions being hedged. In the aggregate, they destroy wealth," Johnson said.
Here's a look at other stories offering insight on ETFs for investors.
Alex Michalka, vice president of investment research at investing platform Wealthfront, said the case for investing in the performance of sports teams is nearly impossible to separate from gambling, since wagering on whether a sports team will win or lose does not facilitate an economic purpose that adds value to the world.
"That is not to say a legitimate economic use case is impossible, but most people will likely use these funds for the same reasons they place a sports bet, which is often to show loyalty to a team or simply for entertainment," Michalka said. "Just because sports betting has an ETF wrapper, it does not change the risk associated with it," Michalka added.
Futures have long been used for hedging, and the CME contracts and FutureSports may be ways for sponsors, broadcasters, insurers and arena vendors to potentially hedge exposure against assets and liabilities. Conceptually, that's similar to an airline hedging fuel prices or an insurer hedging extreme weather risks. But in actuality, that does not apply to the vast majority of investors when it comes to these specific sports investments.
"Sports as an asset class exists, but for a few very select people out there," said Todd Sohn, chief ETF strategist at Baird Strategas. "I'm unsure if 'democratizing' really makes sense here," he said.
He added there are also many risks when it comes to novel ETFs like these with so few buyers in the market with a justifiable economic reason to trade them, risks that range from liquidity to price discovery and manipulation. Insider trading around injuries, trades, and coaching changes; and illiquidity in the investments during the offseason, up to four months of no activity, though trades and free agency can impact outlook, are among them. There should also be the expectations for wide bid/ask spreads and market imbalances with "fan enthusiasm driving prices and no commercial hedgers," Baird Strategas wrote in a preliminary analysis.
Despite the risks, all of which are covered in risk disclosures within these ETFs' prospectuses, Nate Geraci, an ETF expert and president of NovaDius Wealth Management, expects them to be approved by the SEC. Assuming the futures contracts "function properly, and establish sufficient liquidity, I don't see a regulatory reason why the SEC wouldn't approve the ETFs. CME-traded futures held in an ETF wrapper certainly aren't novel, though it's entirely possible the SEC could attempt to classify these sports-focused ETFs as such," he said.
The SEC is currently in the midst of a rulemaking proposal and public comment period covering "novel" ETFs, a move the regulator made after ETF companies filed for prediction markets ETFs.
Geraci is not surprised that ETF issuers are chasing the concept. "It's somewhat ironic that ETFs began as a way to offer low-cost, broad-based exposure to the market and have morphed in recent years into expensive, narrowly focused speculation vehicles. That said, it's a tale as old as time in asset management, where fund issuers rush to package and sell whatever is capturing investors' attention," he said.
Evan Mills, a financial advisor at Scholar Advising, an independent fee-only advisory firm, said it is important to understand the difference between owning a productive asset and making a bet on an outcome.
"If you're buying stock in a business, that stock is tied to revenue, earnings, and cash flow, so it appreciates based on that, as well as demand for the stock," Mills said. Bonds, meanwhile, include a contractual stream of payments, and that's how you make money off them.

articles.title_orig: Early Treatment Support and Real-World Care Gaps
articles.title_zh: Early Treatment Support and Real-World Care Gaps
articles.content_orig:
This episode maps the early weeks of oral zongertinib and the real-world factors that threaten them.
This episode maps the early weeks of oral zongertinib and the real-world factors that threaten them. The panel describes a model in which a clinical pharmacist calls the patient at home to confirm the drug has arrived and review administration, followed by an early advanced practice provider visit with labs, a second visit shortly after, and body imaging within the first few months. Faculty explain how community practices without an embedded thoracic pharmacist can replicate this through pharmacotherapy referrals, virtual visits, and phone outreach, and how pharmacists catch dosing nuances such as weight-based dosing and drug interactions. The discussion then examines why patients stop therapy outside trials, from distance and transportation barriers to unprepared reactions to low-grade diarrhea, and dispels the idea that dose reduction sacrifices efficacy. The episode closes on fragmented community care, where the time from diagnosis to drug in hand can stretch past a month.

articles.title_orig: EVERSANA and Pulse Infoframe Announce Strategic Partnership to Deliver Global Real-World Evidence and HEOR Solutions
articles.title_zh: EVERSANA and Pulse Infoframe Announce Strategic Partnership to Deliver Global Real-World Evidence and HEOR Solutions
articles.content_orig:
Collaboration creates unmatched capabilities in biopharma industry for real world data generation and insights for market access strategy
CHICAGO , Oct. 8, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- EVERSANA , a leading provider of technology enabled, modern commercialization services to the biopharmaceutical industry, today announced a strategic partnership with Pulse Infoframe, a leader in real-world evidence (RWE) generation and intelligence. Through the partnership, EVERSANA will pair its end-to-end commercialization, market access and health economics and outcomes research (HEOR) expertise with Pulse Infoframe's proprietary RWE platform and established evidence-generation capabilities, creating a single, continuous evidence engine for pharmaceutical and medical device companies.
The partnership spans the full arc of evidence generation: global site-network and feasibility assessments, registry and natural history study design, and direct data capture from sites and patients, followed by HTA-grade reporting, global value dossiers, and reimbursement strategy. By designing studies to serve regulators, HTA bodies, and commercial teams alike, EVERSANA and Pulse Infoframe help clients carry a single evidence base from first patient enrolled through launch and beyond.
"Real-world evidence has never been more critical as pharmaceutical companies work to develop the best strategies to bring innovative therapies to patients," said Mark Thierer, Chief Executive Officer, EVERSANA. "By pairing our deep commercial and health economics expertise with Pulse Infoframe's robust registry expertise in complex conditions, including rare disease and oncology, we can bring unmatched solutions to customers to help improve market access."
The partnership offers pharmaceutical and medical device manufacturers a seamless solution for evidence generation from study design and global site-network assessments to sophisticated external control arm methods and Health Technology Assessment (HTA)-grade reporting. By uniting complementary strengths, the collaboration delivers compounding gains in efficiency, data quality, and global scale.
"Our platform was built to generate regulatory-grade evidence directly from sites and patients," said Femida Gwadry-Sridhar (PhD), Chief Executive Officer, Pulse Infoframe. "Working with EVERSANA connects that evidence to the regulatory, reimbursement, and commercial decisions it needs to support, at global scale."
The partnership will be highlighted by EVERSANA and Pulse Infoframe at ISPOR Europe 2026, November 8-11 in Vienna, Austria.
About EVERSANA ® EVERSANA ® is the leading independent provider of global services to the life sciences industry. The company's integrated solutions are rooted in the patient experience and span all stages of the product life cycle to deliver long-term, sustainable value for patients, prescribers, channel partners, and payers. The company serves more than 650 organizations, including innovative start-ups and established pharmaceutical companies, to advance life sciences solutions for a healthier world. To learn more about EVERSANA, visit eversana.com .
About Pulse Infoframe Pulse Infoframe is a leading real-world data and evidence generation partner that provides services to clients in the life sciences and healthcare sectors. The company owns and operates its real-world evidence platform, with expertise in registries, natural history studies, and the ability to generate regulatory-grade data directly from sites and patients.

articles.title_orig: Trump interrupted by protesters at Texas rally: ‘They’re paid by enemies of our nation’
articles.title_zh: Trump interrupted by protesters at Texas rally: ‘They’re paid by enemies of our nation’
articles.content_orig:
President Donald Trump made his third trip to Texas in less than a month Wednesday, attacking Democrats and warning about illegal immigration as he stumped for a Senate candidate who’s privately questioned his political capital and whom the president has publicly insulted in personal terms.
Such is the final sprint to the November 3 midterm elections as the GOP faces an increasingly uphill battle to hold on to the Senate, with the path to the majority running through Texas.
Republicans are pouring millions into bolstering state Attorney General Ken Paxton, who polls have shown is facing a closer-than-expected race against Democrat James Talarico in a state Trump carried by more than 13 points in 2024 and that hasn’t elected any Democrats statewide since 1994.
The president’s appearance in San Antonio was vintage Trump, combining lighthearted moments with vicious attacks on his opponents. He joked about his own thinning hair and falsely attacked Talarico as a vegan – noting his wife had told him recently he had been mispronouncing the word. At least a dozen protesters, who interrupted Trump’s rally on several occasions, were removed from the event.
President Donald Trump was forced to stop his speech again and again during a rally in San Antonio, Texas, after a number of protesters disrupted the event.
At one point, Trump appeared to try to clarify incendiary remarks he made earlier this week that drew harsh bipartisan backlash when he seemed to suggest Iran could “take out” Los Angeles and San Diego.
Speaking at the rally, Trump made similar comments, this time adding, “We’re not going to let that happen.”
One Texas GOP strategist said the event’s effectiveness will be closely watched in the coming days for whether it can improve Paxton’s standing — which could determine continued investment in the state.
The president’s latest Texas trip — which comes less than a week after his last stop here — is part of an aggressive midterm travel blitz that has taken him to traditional red strongholds he overwhelmingly won two years ago, including Alabama, Oklahoma and Nebraska. The president has repeatedly told his rally crowds to “pretend” he’s on the ballot this fall, and his advisers believe their best hope for November is boosting base turnout .
But some Republicans , even in these red states, are looking for distance from the unpopular president. Texas Gov. Greg Abbott will not be at Trump’s Wednesday evening rally, citing scheduling conflicts. He skipped last week’s Trump appearance too.
“It’s pretty clear to me the Paxton team has made the calculation that they believe it’s absolutely worth it,” the Texas GOP strategist said.
Paxton is also making headlines for seeming to blame the president and some of his agenda for his struggles.
The GOP nominee told a group of donors and lobbyists last month that the Iran war and high gas prices are hurting his campaign, according to audio obtained by Axios on Wednesday. “I don’t make the decisions, and I don’t … know what’s behind some of the decisions,” he said, according to Axios. CNN has not independently verified the audio.
Paxton’s campaign dismissed the story. “The Attorney General said what every Texan already knows: gas and diesel prices are too high, and hardworking Texans are struggling at the pump and at the grocery store,” spokeswoman Madison Cercy told CNN in a statement, adding that Trump “is doing everything he can to bring prices down.”
But that followed The New York Times last week publishing audio of Paxton complaining that Trump’s midterm convention, held last month in Dallas, wasn’t helpful.
“So to be honest with you, the numbers — when we did that convention — it dropped our numbers,” the Texas attorney general said. In a statement to CNN, Paxton senior adviser Nick Maddux called the Times story “manipulated nonsense” to “create a story that doesn’t exist.”
Paxton has been plagued by his own set of scandals , including securities fraud charges, which ended in a pre-trial agreement; allegations of infidelity; and a 2023 impeachment in the state House (the Senate acquitted him). But that baggage didn’t stop Trump from backing Paxton over incumbent Sen. John Cornyn in a primary runoff earlier this year.
Their relationship, however, has appeared fraught, even as Trump told reporters in the Oval Office earlier Wednesday that he has no regrets about backing Paxton.
At a stop in Denton, Texas, last week, the president called Paxton “one of the most loyal people” — but also “a pain in the ass sometimes.”
Then there’s his frequent ribbing of the state attorney general’s appearance.
“Some may not like the way he dresses,” Trump said during a speech at the Dallas convention: “I don’t.”
Trump did not repeat that refrain Wednesday night, calling Paxton a “fantastic man” as the two showcased warm relations on stage.
“I’m very proud of him and I think he’s gonna be an unbelievable senator,” Trump said as he invited Paxton to speak.
Paxton, in turn, expressed gratitude to his guest. “Aren’t you guys glad he came to San Antonio?” he asked an enthusiastic crowd.
The president “understands how important Texas is to efforts to try to keep the Senate in Republican control, so I think he can put all that aside and probably focus on the bigger picture,” said one Texas GOP operative unaffiliated with the Paxton campaign, granted anonymity to speak freely.
“But I’m sure he enjoys making Paxton squirm at the same time,” the operative added.
Asked about the candidate’s relationship with Trump earlier Wednesday, Paxton’s campaign pointed to his planned appearance on stage with the president.
Paxton’s comments reported by the Times underscore how the president’s unpopularity — his approval rating is 34% in the latest CNN Poll of Polls — may make him an unwelcome guest for some candidates.
And he is losing support among a group that helped propel him to victory in 2024. His approval rating among Latino voters was just 27%, according to a NBC News/Telemundo poll earlier this week. Trump may be looking to turn that tide with his visit to San Antonio, where the population is 64.6% Hispanic or Latino.
Trump sought to juice turnout among his MAGA base Wednesday evening with a focus on border security and other red meat issues, including the attack on Talarico as a vegan — a claim the Democrat has denied. And there were visible efforts to organize, including information about early voting and mail-in ballots for attendees on screens and in handouts.
But Trump’s visit, the Texas Republican strategist said, comes with its own risk.
“Why go where you can potentially motivate the other side, rather than going to places like Lubbock or Amarillo or East Texas, where you can try to use that brand to actually motivate, you know, the type of voter that needs to turn out for Paxton to win?” the strategist said.
And Democrats see Trump’s return to Texas as a good sign for their side.
“If you have to pull in Donald Trump four times in the closing stretch of the campaign in Texas, then you have given up on independent voters. This is a loss mitigation strategy,” said one Texas Democratic operative.
The Senate race — and the GOP primary and runoff leading up to it — is already on track to be one of the nation’s most expensive.
The GOP-aligned bill in Texas is expected to exceed $300 million, with the party and its affiliated groups outspending Democrats by more than 5-to-1, CNN has previously reported . Since the end of the GOP runoff in late May, Republicans have spent $158 million on ads, with an additional $38 million in upcoming ad reservations, according to the ad tracking firm AdImpact. Democrats, meanwhile, have spent about half that: $75 million on ads between late May and Tuesday, with $6 million reserved.
But that level of spending in deep-red Texas comes with consequences for the rest of the Senate map.
