articles.title_orig: Gov. DeSantis declares state of emergency for 25 Florida counties due to Hurricane Isaias
articles.title_zh: Gov. DeSantis declares state of emergency for 25 Florida counties due to Hurricane Isaias
articles.content_orig:
Hurricane Isaias is now the first hurricane of the 2026 Atlantic hurricane season as it moves toward a landfall on the northern Gulf Coast Friday night or Saturday, with storm surge, rainfall flooding and high winds. It will then spread its heavy rain inland over the East this weekend.
(MORE: Tropical Storm Isaias maps tracker )
Isaias is centered in the Gulf over 400 miles south-southwest of New Orleans, moving east-northeast.
It's expected to rapidly strengthen to at least a Category 2 by Thursday night in the central Gulf.
(MORE: Florida declares state of emergency for 25 counties )
Set The Weather Company as a 'Preferred Source' to get quicker access to the news you value.
Here are the latest watches from the National Hurricane Center, visible on the graphic below:
Storm surge warning : Mouth of the Mississippi River to Steinhatchee, Florida. A storm surge watch extends south to Yankeetown, Florida.
Hurricane warning: Ocean Springs, Mississippi, to the Bay/Gulf County Line in Florida.
Tropical storm warning : Jefferson/Plaquemines Parish line south of New Orleans to west of Ocean Springs, Mississippi, and east of the Bay/Gulf County Line to the Aucilla River, Florida. These warnings also extend to much of inland southern Alabama and parts of southeast Mississippi north of any hurricane watches.
( MORE: What all these tropical terms mean )
Isaias will move toward the northeast through Thursday, before it speeds up and curls northward toward the Gulf Coast.
You can see in the computer model forecast tracks below that the most likely landfall location for Isaias is somewhere from the western Florida Panhandle to the Mississippi Gulf Coast late Friday or early Saturday.
Beyond that, Isaias will get pushed far inland over the Southeast.
Much of the storm's impacts will likely be along and east of its path.
(MORE: What you need to know during hurricane season )
Isaias will first benefit from Gulf water temperatures well into the 80s and a moist air mass, both favorable for intensification over the next day or so.
But with the jet stream sagging far to the south, Isaias will have to battle wind shear.
That matters because wind shear is hostile for both developing and active tropical systems.
You can see the wind shear forecast below; the colors in darker purple and white indicate strong wind shear.
Since the wind shear is expected to become stronger the farther north Isaias goes, it is likely to lose some wind intensity closer to landfall.
For now, the most likely intensity near landfall is a Category 2 hurricane.
The most significant impacts will be felt along and to the east of the storm's track and its inland remnant. That includes where storm surge flooding, strong winds and isolated tornadoes could be felt near the Gulf Coast before and some time after landfall.
The map below shows how much inundation of normally dry ground may occur near the coast from water pushing in from the Gulf as the center of Isaias moves ashore later Friday into early Saturday, according to the National Hurricane Center.
These values represent the peak flood levels if the storm surge happens around high tide.
Damaging winds are most possible in areas covered by hurricane and tropical storm alerts, shown in the graphic near the top of this article, from extreme southeast Louisiana and southern Mississippi to the Florida Panhandle.
Strong winds may pick up as soon as midday Friday and continue at least through Saturday morning.
Downed trees, power lines and power outages that could last for hours or multiple days, are possible in these areas.
Heavy rain from Isaias could arrive along the Gulf Coast as soon as Friday, then will push far inland through the rest of the weekend.
As much as 10 inches of rain could fall locally near the Gulf Coast, with most receiving between 3 and 7 inches.
Locally flooding rainfall is possible over most of the Southeast, Appalachians, and parts of the Ohio Valley and mid-Atlantic this weekend.
As often the case with landfalling hurricanes, there is a threat for tornadoes in outer rainbands as the center approaches land Friday, then possibly again Saturday in parts of the Southeast.
If you're near the Gulf Coast, from southeast Louisiana to Florida, monitor the latest forecast for this system and have your hurricane plans ready to go.
Know if you live in an evacuation zone and what your evacuation route is, if requested to do so by local officials.
Be prepared for power outages that could last at least several hours, or possibly multiple days.
If you're in the Southeast, including the Appalachians, Ohio Valley and mid-Atlantic, be on the lookout for flash flooding this weekend. Avoid flood-prone areas and never drive into flooded stretches of roads.
Impact risk The map below shows the general risk from Isaias and its inland remnant, including from rainfall flooding, winds and storm surge near the coast. This map will update throughout the duration of the storm. The impact levels on the map mean:
(MORE: Stay prepared this hurricane season )
Isaias ( ees-ah-EE-ahs) is one of the trickier names to pronounce on this year's list. To hear the correct pronunciation, listen here .
Isaias replaced "Ike" on one of the Atlantic names lists after that name was retired following the destructive, deadly 2008 hurricane .
It wasn't used during its first year of eligibility in 2014, since we only reached the eighth name, Hanna, that year.
However, the name was used in 2020 for a storm that eventually tracked up the East Coast with destructive winds.
While El Niño continues to shred some systems before they form and weaken the ones that do, three storms have battled the conditions to actually get names and impact the Gulf Coast states. These storms may have not been hurricanes, but they did bring heavy rainfall to the region.
All systems like this one need is a window of opportunity with relatively less wind shear, even in El Niño-assisted conditions.
The tracks of Tropical Storms Arthur, Bertha and Edouard.
Tropical Storm Arthur was a brief June storm that quickly reached tropical storm strength right before a Texas landfall.
The low fell apart quickly after moving onshore, but its remnants brought torrential rainfall over the Gulf Coast. Arthur actually brought 37.53 inches to Alexandria, Louisiana, which was the wettest rainfall total caused by an Atlantic tropical cyclone.
In July, Tropical Storm Bertha formed in the northeast quadrant of the Gulf.  It moved to the north before interestingly turning west and striking the Biloxi Wildlife Management Area in St. Bernard Parish Wednesday afternoon on July 22. Rainfall totals of 1 to 5 inches were widespread with isolated totals exceeding 5 inches.
The next storm to impact the Gulf was Tropical Storm Edouard, which made landfall on Sept. 1, 2026. Winds were around 60 mph at the time of landfall and heavy rainfall was also reported.
Even though this hurricane season has proved to be one of the quietest on record, that doesn’t mean we can’t get an impactful tropical system or hurricane.
There have been seasons in the past that have managed to produce strong storms despite a strong El Niño.
The image below shows several hurricanes that have formed during super El Niño seasons from 1972 to 2015.
Selected hurricanes to have occurred during super El Niño Atlantic hurricane seasons (1972, 1982, 1997, 2015). Portions of tracks at hurricane and Category 3 and higher intensities are color coded. Note: We omitted 1991 since the El Niño did not reach the super criterion until the three-month period centered on December 1991. Other storms during these years are shown with white tracks.

articles.title_orig: British diplomats to remain at scaled-down mission in Jerusalem
articles.title_zh: British diplomats to remain at scaled-down mission in Jerusalem
articles.content_orig:
JERUSALEM — Britain said on Thursday its nearly 200-year-old consulate in Jerusalem would remain operating at a smaller scale, renamed as the “UK Mission” in the city, after Israel ordered ​it shut in a dispute over sanctions on settlements .
Israel last month issued a 30-day deadline for ‌Britain to close the consulate after London announced sanctions targeting Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank, a dispute that has strained relations between the longtime allies. The deadline expired on Thursday.
Gideon Saar, Israel’s foreign minister, said in a statement that the consulate, in east Jerusalem , would ​formally end operations but that some British diplomats would be allowed to continue work in the building under ​a deal struck between Israel and Britain.
Saar’s British counterpart, Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband, said his ⁠country does not accept that Israel has the legal right to close the consulate. The consulate is in a ​part of the city Israel captured in a 1967 war, which Israel later annexed in a move that most countries do ​not recognize.
Miliband said that following discussions with Israel, “our Consulate General building will not be closing, and will be known as the UK Mission, Jerusalem from today.”
Miliband said the UK Mission would continue to “deliver vital services and our work with the Palestinian people.”
Earlier on Thursday, Reuters journalists saw workers in the consulate remove a plaque reading “British Consulate General” and another sign for its ​consular section. The British flag was still flying over the building.
Israel last month ordered Britain to close the consulate within 30 days and ‌remove its ⁠diplomats from the city, after Britain announced sanctions targeting Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank, including a trade ban on goods made there.
The United Nations and most countries consider the Israeli settlements to be illegal under international law. Israel disputes this.
Israel has been adamant the consulate will close even as Britain sought to keep it open, including sending the country’s top ​national security adviser to Israel ​last week for talks.
Britain’s consulate ⁠was founded in 1839, long before the State of Israel was established in 1948. The closure order does not affect Britain’s embassy in Tel Aviv, which handles diplomatic relations with ​Israel’s government.
The consulate, in the Sheikh Jarrah neighborhood of east Jerusalem, handles Britain’s relations with ​Palestinians in ⁠Jerusalem, as well as in the West Bank and Gaza. It also provides consular services to Palestinians.
The British sanctions announcement, and Israel’s order to close the consulate, mark a new low in a relationship that has deteriorated over the past three years. ⁠Britain has ​repeatedly criticized Israel over its actions in the war in Gaza and ​over Israeli settler attacks on Palestinians in the West Bank.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s government, which faces an election later this month, has accused Britain’s governing Labour ​Party of being hostile towards Israel.

articles.title_orig: California Could Become First State to Ban Quartz Countertop Production Amid Health Concerns
articles.title_zh: California Could Become First State to Ban Quartz Countertop Production Amid Health Concerns
articles.content_orig:
California regulators are expected to consider an emergency ban on manufactured stone containing more than 1% crystalline silica in October
Nearly 600 California countertop workers developed silicosis between 2019 and 2026, with 65 needing lung transplants, PEOPLE previously reported
Many workers are developing silicosis, which has no cure and can be fatal after workers inhale crystalline silica dust
California could soon become the first state to ban quartz countertops amid mounting health concerns.
California’s Occupational Safety and Health Standards Board is expected to pass a ban as an emergency regulation this October, The New York Times reported. The board initially began working on the piece of legislation in May, and it would focus on manufactured stone that contains more than 1 percent of crystalline silica.
“The Petitioner states that this action is necessary in light of the continuing epidemic of silicosis that is causing disabling disease and death among California fabrication workers as a result of their workplace exposure to silica dust from engineered stone containing crystalline silica and will open the market for safer products, which are already commercially available,” a petition from the Western Occupational and Environmental Medicine Association (WOEMA) reads.
The petition proposes that the solution to preventing these health conditions is to eliminate “hazardous products and substitution with safer and less toxic materials.”
According to a report from the California Department of Public Health published in August, nearly 600 people in California fell ill with a deadly lung disease after working for manufacturers of the quartz countertops.
Per the report, the number of cases of silicosis has drastically increased in recent years. Between January 2019 and June 2026, health officials identified 592 cases of silicosis among quartz countertop fabrication workers. Of those cases, 65 patients required lung transplants and 31 patients died, PEOPLE previously reported.
Silicosis is a long-term lung disease caused by inhaling very tiny crystalline particles of silicon dioxide, or silica, according to the Cleveland Clinic . Exposure to silica is often work-related and typically seen in fields like construction, stonework, mining, pottery and more. Silicosis has no cure, and can be fatal.
Should the ban pass, Cal-OSHA and the California Department of Industrial Relations, which has also supported the ban, would be acknowledging that the state’s legal regulations surrounding the hazardous materials have failed to protect workers, per The Times.

“The standards board’s decision reflects the urgent need to protect workers from a product that has proven uniquely hazardous,” Denisse Gómez, a spokeswoman for the California Department of Industrial Relations, told the outlet.
PEOPLE has reached out to Cal-OSHA.

articles.title_orig: For France’s Resurgent Far Left, Student Protests Are an Opening and a Threat
articles.title_zh: For France’s Resurgent Far Left, Student Protests Are an Opening and a Threat
articles.content_orig:
Demonstrators have rejected a promise by Sébastien Lecornu to present a plan to fix the country’s education system by the end of the month
French education minister Édouard Geffray has invited the three leading high school students associations for further talks at the ministry later this afternoon.
This comes as a recent opinion poll showed that the French public broadly supports the protest – with three-thirds agreeing with the students’ demands, and 55% backing the demonstrations – but is divided on whether they should continue ( Europe Live, yesterday ).
Aisha Down in London, Joseph Gedeon in Washington and Jennifer Rankin in Brussels
In other news, the Trump administration pressured multiple countries to withdraw their sponsorship of a leading European conference on disinformation, with Canada, Lithuania and the EU’s diplomatic service subsequently agreeing to do so, the Guardian understands.
The conference, #Disinfo2026, taking place Wednesday and Thursday, is the annual meetup of Europe’s counter-disinformation community and has drawn hundreds of researchers, journalists, technologists and policymakers to a hotel in Vilnius, Lithuania. It is run by an independent Brussels non-profit, EU Disinfo Lab.
Days before the conference, the logos of its main supporters – the Lithuanian ministry of foreign affairs, the European External Action Service (EEAS) and Global Affairs Canada, the country’s foreign ministry – were wiped off its website.
Photos of the event shared with the Guardian also show white stickers affixed over the logos of these organisations printed on official conference materials, appearing to indicate they were struck from the program in haste.
Three persons familiar with the matter, including European officials, confirmed that the US state department had been in touch with multiple governments over their support for the conference.
Internal state department documents seen by the Guardian also show US officials thanking Lithuania for “taking US concerns seriously”. The document says Washington was “grateful” Lithuania supposedly found a panel framing the US as a foreign information threat “reprehensible and surprising” and welcomed its decision to limit involvement in the conference.
French education minister Édouard Geffray has invited the three leading high school students associations for further talks at the ministry later this afternoon.
This comes as a recent opinion poll showed that the French public broadly supports the protest – with three-thirds agreeing with the students’ demands, and 55% backing the demonstrations – but is divided on whether they should continue ( Europe Live, yesterday ).
High school protests across France show no sign of slowing down, with nearly 400 educational establishments facing disruptions this morning.
Demonstrators have rejected a promise by prime minister Sébastien Lecornu to present a plan to fix the country’s education system by the end of the month, demanding he fully engages with their demands sooner than that.
In a televised address last night, Lecornu said the country could not be “indifferent” to their concerns, and acknowledged that their anger “does not come from nowhere,” but did not make any immediate headline-grabbing announcements.
“ We want real action, and until we get it, we’ll keep mobilising,” a high school student named Marilou in Fontainebleau told AFP.
I will keep an eye on today’s events in France as they unfold.
Over in Spain , I will look at reactions after last night’s death of María del Carmen Abascal, the 87-year-old whose eviction set off a nationwide wave of protests against Spain’s housing crisis.
Elsewhere, Britain’s prime minister Andy Burnham will meet with Germany’s Friedrich Merz in Berlin for political talks. Unusually, however, the pair will not hold a joint press conference.
It’s Thursday, 8 October 2026 , it’s Jakub Krupa here, and this is Europe Live .

articles.title_orig: 87-year-old Maricarmen dies in hospital after infamous eviction ordeal
articles.title_zh: 87-year-old Maricarmen dies in hospital after infamous eviction ordeal
articles.content_orig:
María del Carmen Abascal, the 87-year-old woman whose eviction from her longtime Madrid home sparked nationwide protests across Spain and unleashed a political crisis in the country culminating in the government calling for snap elections, died on Wednesday while hospitalised.
Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez led the way on social media offering his condolences after housing activists and Abascal's lawyer announced her death. Known widely as “Maricarmen,” she had become a symbol for renters struggling with Spain's housing affordability crisis.
“All my love to Maricarmen’s family and loved ones,” Sánchez wrote in a post on X. “A hug as well to all of us who feel this loss as our own today. Rest in peace.”
The emotions ran into anger on the street among the protesters gathered near Spain's Parliament who chanted “Maricarmen lives, the fight goes on!”
“A great deal of sorrow. And above all, the thought that she is the cause, the head of this whole revolution that has happened, and that she can’t see it,” said Iciar López, a 32-year-old psychologist and protester in the capital Madrid.
“It makes me very sad that she can’t see if anything comes of it. That’s what angers me the most, honestly.”
Spaniards increasingly frustrated by housing costs periodically march in major cities demanding action from lawmakers.
But a fresh wave of indignation has swept the Iberian nation since 23 September, when Maricarmen, who used a wheelchair, was carried on a stretcher from her home of seven decades after police cordoned off the street and removed protesters.
She was taken to a hospital because of her fragile health. Televised images of the eviction prompted thousands of people to protest in Madrid and other cities across the country.
Maricarmen's lawyer, Beatriz Duro, did not disclose the cause of death when she confirmed it to Cadena Ser radio. Duro said that she and the activists were all devastated.
“Maricarmen's case, which captured media attention and travelled around the world, leaves us the image of the shameful violence of these types of evictions and the impact they can have on people’s health,” said Duro.
She had been expected to return home after leaving the hospital. The real estate company that evicted her in order to rent the property at a much higher price eventually caved in under immense public pressure and agreed to let her return to the apartment.
“Although a historic agreement was reached that would have allowed her to return home, this solution came too late,” the Madrid Tenants' Union said in a statement on Wednesday. “It was an entirely avoidable situation following a harrowing ordeal.”
The average rent for Spain has almost doubled in the last 10 years. The government said that 26% of Spaniards who rent housing spend an average of 40% of their income on rent and utilities, compared with the European Union average of 18% of renters who do so.
Protesters camped in Madrid’s central Puerta del Sol square held a minute of silence after learning of her death.
Maricarmen spent almost her entire life in her apartment, where she first lived with her parents and brother. She later worked as a secretary for the board of a pharmaceutical company, according to Spanish media outlets.
After retiring in 1998, she spent her days walking around the neighbourhood, running errands and taking care of the precious items in her home.
Spanish media reported that black-and-white family photographs were among the only things she had brought with her to the hospital.
“Maricarmen only wanted to die in her home. She wasn’t asking for anything else,” Eugenio Melchor, 22, said at the protest in Madrid.
“She was dying in her home and she almost did. They have killed her. I mean, there’s no other word for it, and I hope those responsible for this pay and go to trial.”

articles.title_orig: Tropical Storm Isaias forms in Gulf, could reach U.S. as hurricane this weekend. See maps, possible path.
articles.title_zh: Tropical Storm Isaias forms in Gulf, could reach U.S. as hurricane this weekend. See maps, possible path.
articles.content_orig:
Update: Isaias became a hurricane late Wednesday night. See the latest forecast here .
Tropical Storm Isaias was "quickly intensifying" and is expected to approach the U.S. Gulf Coast on Friday after becoming a hurricane, according to the National Hurricane Center .
Currently swirling in the Gulf, Isaias would be the Atlantic basin's first hurricane of the season and is its ninth named storm. An El Niño climate pattern continues to bring a more active season in the Pacific. The storm formed with less than two months remaining in the 2026 hurricane season , which ends Nov. 30.
Tropical Storm Isaias, which grew from Tropical Depression Nine on Wednesday and is pronounced "ees-ah-EE-ahs," is expected to pass to the north of Mexico's Yucatan Peninsula on Thursday and make landfall along the northern Gulf Coast of the U.S. late Friday or early Saturday, the hurricane center said.
A hurricane warning was issued Wednesday for the northern Gulf Coast, from Ocean Springs, Mississippi, to Florida's Bay/Gulf county line, and a tropical storm warning was issued from Louisiana's Jefferson/Plaquemines Parish line to Ocean Springs, and from the Bay/Gulf county line to Florida's Aucilla River. A storm surge warning was also issued from the mouth of the Mississippi River to Yankeetown, Florida, according to the hurricane center.
Tropical storm-force winds were extending outward up to 60 miles from the storm's center on Wednesday evening. Its maximum sustained winds were 70 mph, and it was forecast to become a hurricane by Thursday morning, the hurricane center said.
A storm's maximum wind speed must rise to at least 74 mph to be considered a hurricane.
Isaias is forecast to bring moderate to heavy rainfall to the Gulf Coast and into the rest of the Southeast this weekend into early next week. The hurricane center forecasts 3 to 7 inches of rain and as much as 10 inches in some places on the central Gulf Coast from southeastern Louisiana to the Florida Panhandle. Much of the Southeast, and as far north as the Tennessee Valley and the Carolinas, could see rainfall ranging from 1 to 5 inches, forecasters said.
Some longer-range forecast models also see this moisture eventually reaching the Ohio Valley and Northeast by midweek next week.
The hurricane center on Thursday warned of "an increasing risk of dangerous wind and storm surge impacts" along parts of the northern Gulf Coast and urged people living in Louisiana, Alabama, Mississippi and northern Florida to "closely monitor the latest forecast updates and ensure they have their hurricane plan in place."
At high tide, the approximately 300-mile stretch between Ocean Springs, Mississippi, and Indian Pass, Florida, could see a storm surge of up to 7 feet, forecasters said, potentially causing major flooding.
In addition to rain, the hurricane center said Isaias could potentially bring urban flooding and isolated river flooding to places in its path.
Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis on Tuesday signed an executive order declaring a state of emergency for 25 Florida counties ahead of the storm's arrival. DeSantis said in a statement that the order "ensures communities have the time and resources necessary to prepare for potential severe weather impacts to the Panhandle and Big Bend region of Florida."
On Wednesday, Alabama Gov. Kay Ivey issued a similar state of emergency for 40 counties, saying in a statement that it will allow Alabama officials "to take any needed steps ahead of landfall."
While tropical storm and hurricane formation and frequency vary throughout the season, the "I"-named systems tend to be the most retired names within the Atlantic basin.
The most commonly known retired "I"-named storms are Ian (2022), Ida (2021), Irma (2017) and Irene (2011).
When Ike was retired in 2008, Isaias replaced the "I" name on the Atlantic tropical cyclones list, which rotates every six years.

articles.title_orig: Japan ranked best country in the world for fourth straight year
articles.title_zh: Japan ranked best country in the world for fourth straight year
articles.content_orig:
Japan was named the world’s most attractive country for the fourth consecutive year, according to survey results released Wednesday, extending a winning streak as record numbers of overseas visitors continue to flock to the country.
Japan took the top spot in the U.S. edition of the magazine Conde Nast Traveler’s Readers’ Choice Awards for “Best Countries in the World.”
Italy ranked second, followed by Ireland, Cambodia and Spain.
The results demonstrate the country’s enduring appeal among international travelers as inbound tourism continues to surge . A record 42.7 million overseas visitors came to Japan in 2025, according to Justice Ministry figures.
Tokyo’s Haneda Airport was ranked the sixth best in the world, with Singapore’s Changi Airport taking the top place.
In a news release Wednesday, the Japan National Tourism Organization (JNTO) said Japan’s strong showing reflected not only the appeal of its tourism resources, but also qualities distinctive to Japan, such as its hospitality and safety.
“We hope that this continued international recognition will generate even greater interest in Japan and encourage more people to visit,” the organization wrote.
Conde Nast Traveler readers cast 798,867 votes in this year’s awards, the magazine’s 39th edition. The awards, held annually since 1988, rank destinations and travel experiences based on readers’ overall evaluations, with voting across categories including countries, hotels and cruises.
In the magazine’s U.K. edition of the rankings, Japan placed second behind Greece, with Italy, Turkey and Portugal completing the top five. The magazine highlighted the country’s restaurants, hot springs, cherry blossoms and high-speed rail network, as well as its mix of traditional culture, design and technological innovation.
“We will continue to showcase the unique attractions of regions across Japan, including their nature, culture, and cuisine, to audiences around the world, while encouraging travel to regional destinations and working toward sustainable tourism,” JNTO wrote.

articles.title_orig: Naval drone hits oil tanker off Russian resort city Sochi, triggering massive blaze
articles.title_zh: Naval drone hits oil tanker off Russian resort city Sochi, triggering massive blaze
articles.content_orig:
Russian officials said a Liberian-flagged tanker was attacked and a crew of 23 Indian nationals rescued
An oil tanker off Russia’s Black Sea coast was struck by a naval drone, triggering a huge fire and black smoke cloud that blanketed parts of the resort city of Sochi, Russia’s transport ministry has said.
The transport ministry said a Liberian-flagged tanker had been attacked and that “crude oil is burning openly in the waters of the Black Sea”.
“Firefighting efforts will begin once the fire’s intensity has subsided and rescue vessels can safely approach the tanker,” the ministry said.
A crew of 23 – all Indian citizens – had been rescued, it added.
Russia and Ukraine have targeted commercial shipping around the Black Sea since the conflict began, and Russia has recently attacked grain vessels carrying Ukrainian goods near the coast of Romania.
There was no comment from Kyiv on the attack.
Videos and photos circulated on social media from Sochi – a popular Black Sea resort city of almost 500,000 people – showed bright orange flames out at sea and a thick column of black smoke billowing into the sky.
Local officials restricted access to the coast and beaches.
Elsewhere on Tuesday, Bulgaria’s prime minister said that two commercial vessels had been struck by drones in the first attack on shipping in the Nato member’s exclusive economic zone in the Black Sea.
Bulgarian authorities said that the origin of the drones was under investigation, but Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy blamed Russia for the drone strikes. Bulgarian prime minister Rumen Radev condemned the attack.
After an emergency government meeting, Radev said: “This is an unacceptable attack in Bulgaria’s exclusive economic zone. It is a blatant violation of international law and maritime law.”
Sea and aerial drones attacked the ships about 80 miles (128km) off Bulgaria’s coast, he said.
Zelenskyy warned in his nightly address on Tuesday that a “massive strike” from Russia was likely to come, and in the early hours of Wednesday Kyiv was attacked.
Russian strikes damaged buildings and warehouses across the Ukrainian capital, Kyiv’s mayor ​Vitali ‌Klitschko said ‌on Telegram.
Agence France-Presse reported multiple explosions in Kyiv, and Reuters reported two people were killed by Russian strikes.
A separate Russian strike on Ukraine’s south-eastern city of Dnipro damaged ⁠an industrial facility, ​officials said, without giving details.
Kyiv has been under increased attack as winter approaches, with Russian airstrikes targeting energy infrastructure, rail and road transport, including bridges that connect the city over the Dnipro river. Air raid sirens have sounded almost constantly day and night, urging residents to take cover in basements, shelters and subway stations.
With Reuters and Agence France-Presse

articles.title_orig: ByteDance heads first SCMP Plus Going Global 100 ranking
articles.title_zh: ByteDance heads first SCMP Plus Going Global 100 ranking
articles.content_orig:
Social media giant beats out Foxconn Industrial, Shein and BYD in new SCMP Plus ranking of China’s global champions
TikTok owner ByteDance is China’s Going Global champion, according to a new SCMP Plus databank tracking mainland companies’ overseas expansion efforts.
About two-thirds of the Going Global 100 members are technology or consumer companies, such as carmakers, reflecting how private businesses are driving China’s overseas growth through the development of cutting-edge technology and the creation of their own global brands. Private manufacturers are also now outpacing state-owned enterprises (SOEs) in overseas expansion, as they move beyond being assemblers for multinational brands and look to escape cutthroat price wars at home.
“Private firms have started to dominate, given the growing prominence of consumer electronics, e-commerce platforms, digital tech, EVs and green tech and even light manufacturing,” said Jayant Menon, senior fellow at the ISEAS – Yusof Ishak Institute in Singapore.

articles.title_orig: As China and the EU begin crunch trade talks, optimism is in short supply
articles.title_zh: As China and the EU begin crunch trade talks, optimism is in short supply
articles.content_orig:
Observers on both sides are braced for more turbulence – and mainly hope Beijing and Brussels can avoid a full-blown trade conflict
As China and the European Union began a fresh round of trade talks in Beijing on Thursday, observers on both sides appeared to agree on one thing: a big breakthrough was unlikely.
Chinese firms based in Europe said they hoped the talks could achieve some “limited progress” to help stabilise the trade relationship, while European analysts remained cautious about the potential outcome.
“They’re bound to get some results,” said a Chinese source with knowledge of the talks, adding that EU Trade Commissioner Maros Sefcovic “will not go home empty-handed”.
The China Chamber of Commerce to the EU called on both sides to make full use of the Trade and Investment Consultations (TIC) mechanism to manage differences, push for solutions and send clearer signals to businesses.

articles.title_orig: Accused Chinese spy’s crypto cash flow, ‘unfit mother’ claims exposed in court
articles.title_zh: Accused Chinese spy’s crypto cash flow, ‘unfit mother’ claims exposed in court
articles.content_orig:
The Southern California real estate agent accused of spying on a prominent Taiwanese family for China allegedly had access to $190,000 in a secret Chinese crypto account, as allegations surfaced that the she is “an unfit mother” at a court hearing Wednesday.
Wanying Zhang appeared in an LA courthouse wearing a white jumpsuit and shackles alongside new attorney Craig Harbaugh, who asked for home confinement for his client. The government vehemently argued that she was a flight risk.
At the hearing, prosecutors accused Zhang of having access to $190,000 in a secret Chinese cryptocurrency account that she “was still receiving profits from.” They also pointed to Zhang’s brother having ties to the Chinese government.
Prosecutors referenced a seized iCloud video they said would show Zhang was “a danger to society,” arguing that her ties to “her family may not be as strong as they seem” as her husband Edric Ding looked on.
“You should have produced this video and I could say she’s an unfit mother,” Judge Steve Kim said, as it was revealed that Zhang has “young children.”
Prosecutors also pointed to a dozen one-way trips Zhang allegedly took to China, Paris and Japan. Harbaugh argued that purchasing one-way tickets was more economical.
Judge Kim ruled Zhang was a flight risk, and she was taken into custody by US Marshals without bail.
She’s expected back in court on October 19.
Zhang’s initial hearing on Monday took a bizarre turn when her public defender, Chad Pennington, asked for a side conversation with the judge seconds after the proceeding began, leading to a lengthy 20-minute court recess.
When the parties returned, Zhang was asked if she understood what she was accused of and answered “yes.”
The real estate agent was arrested at LAX Sunday after being accused of spying for China. Zhang, also known as “Heather,” was busted as she tried to board a flight to Shanghai.
Video taken shortly after the arrest showed several FBI agents leading the handcuffed Zhang through an airport terminal.
The 34-year-old, who lives in Irvine, is accused of working with handlers from the People’s Republic of China to surveil the son of Taiwan President Ching-te Lai.
Zhang, who worked for a real estate firm along with her husband, allegedly traveled to Seattle in September 2025 to spy on Ting-Yu Lai, an engineer in his 30s who is based in the US.
Surveillance camera photographs also allegedly caught Zhang sitting in a car with an accomplice taking pictures of his house and close relatives.
She appeared to have lived a jet-setting lifestyle before federal authorities detained her.
Zhang documented trips to Paris and outings with friends across the West Coast on her social media pages.
She also appeared to have graduated from USC, where the total cost of attendance can run more than $75,000 per year.
Ding’s social media shows outings to Korean barbecue restaurants, as well as anime and sword-art expos.
The couple is also seen posing with what appears to be their child.
Zhang’s arrest comes amid several other high-profile California cases involving allegations of covert Chinese government activity or influence.
Disgraced former Arcadia mayor Eileen Wang entered a plea in federal court following the bombshell admission she was a spy for China in March.
Former Democratic Rep. Eric Swalwell confessed to a prescription drug-fueled sex romp with a suspected Chinese spy Christine Fang, also known as “Fang Fang,” according to newly released FBI files in August.
“We have a problem with Beijing using Chinese Americans for their own purposes in California,” First Assistant US Attorney Bill Essayli said. “They are using them for their own foreign affairs because they are playing the long game to get a competitive advantage over us.”

articles.title_orig: Donald Trump’s Texas rally rocked by repeated protests
articles.title_zh: Donald Trump’s Texas rally rocked by repeated protests
articles.content_orig:
Trump briefly stepped away from the microphone after one protester appeared to approach the stage
Donald Trump’s latest campaign rally was rocked by repeated protests on Wednesday as the US president urged Texas voters to back embattled Senate candidate Ken Paxton.
At least half a dozen demonstrators interrupted the US president during his remarks in San Antonio, with some led away by police. One was physically assaulted by an older Trump supporter as he tried to leave the arena.
Trump briefly stepped away from the microphone after one protester appeared to approach the stage. “He’s going back home to mom,” the president said after the man was removed. “But what he doesn’t know is his mom voted for Trump.”
Supporters waving cowboy hats and chanting “USA” drowned out some of the protesters, while Trump told demonstrators to “get the hell out of here”. He mocked their appearance and claimed without evidence that “they’re paid by enemies of our nation”.
The president also used Wednesday’s rally to address recent comments in which he appeared to suggest that Iran could destroy Los Angeles or San Diego, earning widespread condemnation from Democrats.
In remarks that were again less than crystal clear, Trump said: “I said it the other day, let them hit a missile into San Diego or Los Angeles on the way. Let them hit – you want to see a horror show? You want to see problems? Let them hit San Diego. Let them hit Los Angeles and you want to see some bad things happen.
“You want to see a country that would be in freefall. We’re not going to let that happen. We protect our cities, we protect our country, we’re not letting that happen. And they’d use it, too. They’d use it.”
Trump was making his third trip to Texas in less than a month as Republicans pour money into races they had expected to win comfortably in November’s midterm elections.
Paxton, whom Trump endorsed during the Republican primary after turning against the incumbent senator John Cornyn, was called on stage by the president and thanked him for his support.
“Mr President, I want to thank you for coming for me, for coming for us, and for coming for Texas,” Paxton said. “We are going to win this race.”
Trump described Paxton as “perhaps the greatest attorney general in the United States of America,” and said: “He was tough and he was with us all the way. He’s a fantastic man.”
The Republican campaign to maintain control of the Senate has become increasingly focused on Texas, where Democrat James Talarico has emerged as a serious threat. A New York Times/ Siena College poll released last weekend showed Talarico leading Paxton 51% to 45% among likely voters. Texas has not elected a Democrat to the Senate since 1988.
Trump won the state by almost 14 percentage points in 2024, but his approval rating has fallen sharply. A Reuters/Ipsos poll completed on Monday put his approval rating at 32%, while registered voters preferred Democrats to Republicans 44%-37%.
Trump’s relationship with Paxton has sometimes appeared uneasy. Trump called Paxton “a pain in the ass sometimes” last week, but on Wednesday did not discuss a leaked recording of Paxton in which the Senate candidate reportedly complained about the war in Iran, rising fuel prices and the way his campaign was being run.
Instead he spent much of the rally attacking Talarico, whom he repeatedly referred to as “Tala-freako”. He claimed without evidence that Talarico is vegan and recently disappeared: “He’s sick because he’s been forced to eat meat for political reasons and he’s throwing up all over the place.”
Trump insisted: “The people of Texas are not going to let weak, gutless, self-hating, transgender-promoting freak shows destroy everything that we’ve built.”
The president’s political difficulties in Texas were underlined by the absence of Republican governor Greg Abbott, a close Trump ally who is himself facing a competitive re-election race against Democratic state representative Gina Hinojosa.
Abbott was instead due to attend the dedication of a hospital about 330 miles away. Democrats seized on his decision not to appear with Trump.
Republicans have now devoted more than $300m to elections in Texas, according to the Associated Press, while Trump’s broader 32-day campaign blitz has taken him through several Republican-leaning states, including Oklahoma, Alabama, Ohio and Nebraska.

articles.title_orig: Cornell defendant is fighting AG Letitia James’ appointment as special prosecutor
articles.title_zh: Cornell defendant is fighting AG Letitia James’ appointment as special prosecutor
articles.content_orig:
One of the seven men named in the lawsuit filed by a former Cornell University student who alleges that she was sexually assaulted at an on-campus fraternity house has filed a petition to block New York Attorney General Letitia James’ appointment as special prosecutor in the case .
The attorney for Gillio Lopes, who has denied that he sexually assaulted the woman, filed a petition in Albany County Supreme Court on Wednesday. His filing says James should not be the prosecutor in the case because she has “unequivocally demonstrated a bias and presumption of guilt against the defendants named in the Civil Case.”
The Article 78 petition, filed against James and Gov. Kathy Hochul, is a proceeding used to challenge an action by a state or local government officer or agencies in New York.
Hochul appointed James last week to independently investigate Jane Doe’s allegations in the lawsuit, in which she says she was plied with alcohol, sexually assaulted and gang-raped at the Chi Phi fraternity house in October 2024. In her role, James will determine whether criminal charges are warranted.
James’ office declined to comment on the Article 78 filing.
In a statement Monday, James said: “My office enforces our state’s laws to protect all New Yorkers. I am committed to leading a comprehensive investigation they can trust, guided only by the facts, the evidence, and the law.”
Hochul’s office reiterated support for James on Wednesday.
Reached for comment on Lopes’ filing, the governor’s office referred to her comments last week.
“I have every confidence in our Attorney General to do what she has always done: look at the facts, examine the record and draw the proper conclusions. That’s exactly what’s going to happen in this case,” Hochul said at the time.
Hochul appointed James after she expressed dismay over Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten’s investigation of Doe’s allegations. He has said his office found a lack of criminality at the time and declined to press charges, but he reopened the case after the lawsuit sparked national uproar.
Jane Doe’s civil suit was filed last month against Cornell, Chi Phi and seven fraternity brothers. None of the men named have been criminally charged.
The fraternity was suspended from campus, and it remains barred.
Cornell said in a statement Sept. 28 that it conducted a thorough, monthslong Title IX investigation in 2024 that handed down “a range of sanctions, which included expulsions and suspensions ” from the university. Two of the fraternity members were expelled, and two others were suspended. A third, who had already graduated, was barred from campus, and the final two were issued no-contact orders and required to write “reflection papers,” according to a source who has seen the written decision of the Title IX investigation.
Lopes’ filing argues that James’ appointment is “improper” and cites a post her office shared on X on Sept. 28 , three days before her appointment was announced. In the post, she said: “What this young woman has been forced to endure is horrific and unacceptable. I’m holding her in my heart and in my prayers. To her, and to all survivors: you’re not alone. We stand with you.”
The post, the petition contends, “made clear that she has formed an opinion about the case” and that “she has already reached the conclusion that Petitioner and the other named Defendants are guilty.”
The petition also seeks to have the court review James’ appointment and asks that her appointment be annulled or modified so she is not personally directing the probe or any resulting prosecution.
Stuart Bernstein, an attorney for Lopes, said Wednesday: “As Governor Hochul has said, the public needs confidence in the individual leading this investigation. AG James, based upon her very public statements validating Jane Doe, certainly doesn’t instill confidence in a fair investigation.”
In her lawsuit, Doe accuses Lopes of kissing her and sexually assaulting her without her consent.
Attorneys for two of the seven men, including Lopes, have denied to NBC News that they sexually assaulted Doe. An attorney for a third man denied the allegations to ABC News. NBC News has not received responses to requests for comment from the other men.
On Tuesday, Andrew Miltenberg, an attorney for Lopes, said he welcomes Cornell’s decision to have an independent review of its handling of Doe’s allegations, which will be led by former acting U.S. Attorney General Sally Yates.
“In our experience, Cornell’s investigations have generally been thorough. That said, we have also seen due process problems that have affected respondents, and on at least two occasions we have gone to federal court to try to address those issues. In this case, we do not agree with the outcome as to Mr. Lopes,” Miltenberg said.
Shayna Jacobs is a national reporter for NBC News digital.
Marlene Lenthang is a breaking news reporter for NBC News Digital.

articles.title_orig: Coco Gauff explained how online harassment "drained" her in China Open
articles.title_zh: Coco Gauff explained how online harassment "drained" her in China Open
articles.content_orig:
By TAMARA PRENN, SENIOR SPORTS REPORTER
Published: 06:30 EDT, 7 October 2026 | Updated: 10:09 EDT, 7 October 2026
Coco Gauff was knocked out of China Open amid concerns over her health one day after the American star highlighted the vile racism she had encountered after being mixed up in a 'cheating' storm against 16-year-old Sun Xinran.
The two-time Grand Slam champion had been 5-4 down in her third-round tie in Beijing when she patted a straightforward volley over the net, which Sun charged up the court to send back for a winner.
But Gauff had thrown up her arms in complaint as the forehand sailed over her head, telling the chair umpire that she had been distracted by a sponsor change on the electronic advertising boards on both sides of the court.
With the point replayed, Gauff wrenched momentum from her opponent and booked her spot in the fourth round - only to struggle from the early stages against world No19 Elise Mertens.
Level on serve at 4-3, Gauff's game unravelled to lose the next six games, with the US star telling her camp with some concern at 4-1 in the second set that she didn't know why she was so low on fighting spirit.
'I have no energy. I'm trying, I have no energy. I can't see the ball, I feel like I'm going to pass out,' she told the team in her player's box. 'I'm going to just try to finish the match.'
Coco Gauff sparked health concerns after revealing she was going to 'pass out' during her defeat by Elise Mertens in China
In the build-up to the match the US star had to contend with vile racism on social media after she requested a replayed point in her third-round match against Sun Xinran
Gauff eventually lost 6-3, 6-3, downed in straight sets for the first time since February.
After the match, Gauff admitted that the events of the previous day had taken their toll.
'It has been kind of draining, I'm not going to lie,' she said. 'I just turn off my phone and move on. There's nothing you can do.
'I think today I was just a bit flat. I just didn't play well. I think I wasn't moving well. There were a lot of things I didn't do well.'
The 22-year-old's preparations were marred in the build-up as she struggled in the face of racist abuse on social media in the wake of her controversial point against Sun.
Sharing a statement to clarify when she had stopped the match as she had done, Gauff sought to set the record straight after being accused that she had only protested due to her low-quality volley.
Gauff cited a flicker at the beginning of the point which she admitted she wasn't sure 'if that is what I actually saw'.
Continuing, the former US Open champion wrote: 'We are told before the matches we are allowed to continue to finish play so KEEP IT [in] MIND I am thinking about all this while I'm playing the point.
'Anything can be challenged after the point is over (as in most sports you can review a call after the play is over, I personally think this is the correct rule). If I would've lost the point my opponent is also free to do the same thing and ask for a replay and she would've been completely in her right to do so.
'When it flickered again I raised my hands before she hit her shot because this is when I was sure I saw the light flicker and it wasn't my mind doing tricks lol (which again doesn't matter because anything can be challenged after the point).
'It was an unfortunate situation but it is out of my control, the think pieces and calling me unfair is ridiculous when those are the rules. I did not make them, I think it's weird I'm getting hate for following the rules.
Gauff told reporters of the toll the cheating storm had taken on her after her defeat
'Xinran is [an] incredible talent and player, I apologized for the situation at the end of the match and she completely understood. I did not like to see her so emotional as I've been there and I really understand what it is like but this is just the beginning of an incredible career.
'It was an honor to share the court in front of her home crowd.'
She also highlighted the level of racism she is subject to on social media, with her reply coming to a commenter who had written 'f*** you' to her and called her the n-word.
'Hey everyone,' Gauff replied, amplifying the comment. 'You can dislike me or disagree about what happened without being racist.
'The amount of racist comments/dms I've received in the last few hours is insane. Lastly, I'm not a cheater or a thief.'
Gauff received an outpouring of support from fans in the wake of the racist abuse on social media, which was later limited after violating X's rules against hateful conduct.

articles.title_orig: Bringing local models and sandboxed tools to Windows and GitHub Copilot
articles.title_zh: Bringing local models and sandboxed tools to Windows and GitHub Copilot
articles.content_orig:
Coming soon, GitHub Copilot will determine when a task is best handled by on-device intelligence and when it should leverage cloud-scale models.
When leveraging agents, developers need both choice and control. They need technologies that offer clear boundaries for their agents and make it easy to choose the model with the right speed, performance, and cost profile for each task. That’s why GitHub offers frontier models from major model providers, as well as options like Project HydraFusion , an orchestrator choosing one or multiple models for each task while balancing performance, cost, and latency. It’s also why Windows has developed Microsoft Execution Containers (MXC) to help secure interactive and non-interactive agentic coding sessions.
Coming by the end of the month, GitHub Copilot will determine when a task is best handled by on-device intelligence and when it should leverage cloud-scale models. Rather than forcing developers to manage infrastructure decisions themselves, GitHub Copilot automatically coordinates local and cloud inference behind the scenes. For NVIDIA RTX Spark Windows PCs like Surface Laptop Ultra, that means we are enabling local coding in GitHub Copilot with powerful local inference models and hardware capable of delivering a great experience at the edge.
The result is poised to be the next step in the HydraFusion vision: intelligent orchestration that spans not just multiple models, but multiple compute environments including the edge. GitHub Copilot can run commands in these environments with controlled access to files, networks, system capabilities, and credentials. Developers can automate with confidence and security in mind.
Local inference starts with a memory budget. Surface Laptop Ultra is built around NVIDIA RTX Spark, with up to 128 GB of unified memory and up to 1 petaflop of AI compute.
With a discrete GPU, dedicated video memory is an important constraint: moving model data between system memory and the GPU can add overhead. Unified memory gives the CPU and GPU access to a shared physical pool. That makes more capacity available to the workload, but it doesn’t make all of it available to model weights.
The operating system, your applications, and the inference runtime need memory, too. So does the key-value cache, which stores attention state for tokens the model has already processed. As an agent reads files and receives tool results, its context can grow, increasing memory use and the work needed to process the next request.
Keeping a model loaded between requests can avoid repeated loading work. However, it doesn’t guarantee constant response time; context length, memory pressure, and the rest of the workload still matter. That’s why the useful question isn’t just whether a model fits, but how it behaves over a complete coding task.
To bring this local-development experience to life, Microsoft AI developed a local version of MAI Code 1.1 Flash, a coding-optimized mixture-of-experts model with 137 billion total and 6.8 billion active parameters. The on-device work applies quantization and speculative decoding to reduce the model footprint and improve end-to-end responsiveness while preserving the task completion and tool-use quality that matter in an agent loop.
Quantization reduces the precision used to represent model weights and activations, lowering memory requirements. Because code doesn’t degrade gracefully, the release evaluation must measure coding-task success as well as footprint: a single incorrect token can produce a syntax error, wrong identifier, malformed tool call, or broken diff.
Speculative decoding trades additional working memory for higher decode throughput and lower end-to-end latency. A drafter proposes candidate token blocks and the target model verifies them.
For a coding agent, the important tradeoff is whether the smaller model can still complete the same tasks. A smaller footprint is useful only if changes in code quality and tool use are understood.
With our first shipping version of MAI Code 1.1 Flash on Surface Laptop Ultra we achieve the following performance at different context lengths, with peak memory usage of 75.5GB at 256k context. At 64k and 128k context, prompt-processing throughput reaches 923.5 and 769.8 tokens per second, respectively.
The quantized version of MAI Code 1.1 Flash we use on device retains capability impressively compared to the Bfloat16 cloud variant, coming in at 53GB, an 80% reduction in size.
GitHub Copilot is adding two ways to use local models across the GitHub Copilot CLI, Copilot app, and VS Code. Developers can let Copilot’s intelligent Auto orchestration choose when to use local or cloud inference, or they can explicitly select a local model for workflows that require direct control.
With Auto, developers do not need to decide where each task should be run. Across a multi-turn session, Copilot can consider task context and cache state as it routes work between local and cloud models, preserving useful, cached work as the session evolves.
This orchestrated experience complements direct model selection, giving developers a choice between letting Copilot optimize model placement and choosing a specific local model themselves.
Explicit local-model selection supports workflows that need a specific provider, model, or endpoint. Developers can select MAI Code 1.1 Flash through the Windows ML provider or connect GitHub Copilot to OpenAI-compatible local endpoints and choose from the models those endpoints expose.
An agent’s shell commands normally inherit the access of the account running them. Moving inference onto the device doesn’t change that. Sandboxing applies a policy to the processes and local services the agent launches, controlling access to files, networks, credentials, system capabilities, and execution paths regardless of which model requested the work.
GitHub Copilot uses Microsoft Execution Containers , or MXC, an open-source library from the Windows team that translates policy into native operating-system controls. On Windows, GitHub Copilot uses the BaseContainer tier of the ProcessContainer backend. On macOS, it uses Seatbelt. On Linux, it uses bubblewrap . These local backends don’t require a separate virtual machine or container image, but we plan to make them options available through MXC in the future.
When sandboxing is enabled, shell commands and, by default, local Model Context Protocol servers and language servers run inside the process boundary. Built-in file tools run inside GitHub Copilot itself: the agent harness checks their requests against the effective policy, but those checks aren’t OS-enforced child-process isolation. Remote MCP servers are also outside the local process sandbox; when MCP sandbox controls apply, GitHub Copilot checks their connection policy in process.
Opening the GitHub Copilot CLI and running `/sandbox` slash command allows you to configure your settings at any time.
To show how these technologies work together, let’s use a real-world example.
Consider a job that reads local repositories, runs their tests in working copies, and writes one HTML report each morning. The source repositories should remain read-only, and the test processes shouldn’t access the network. Model selection is independent: the same job can use a configured local or cloud model.
Open the settings dialog by clicking the gear icon in the GitHub Copilot app and selecting your project in the left menu. For this example, we’ll be using the `copilot-sdk` repo that hosts our opensource GitHub Copilot Runtime/SDK project.
Enabling the `Sandbox new sessions` toggle turns on sandboxing by default whenever you work within that project. By default, it’s current working directly is read/write while the rest of the system remains largely read-only or inaccessible to an agent.
Select the` Automations` section on the left navigation and click the `Start automation` button to open the dialog that allows you to configure a new automation.
Aft

articles.title_orig: World Health Organization says Russian lab worker’s death has not been clearly linked to plague
articles.title_zh: World Health Organization says Russian lab worker’s death has not been clearly linked to plague
articles.content_orig:
Frank McGeorge, MD , Local 4's Medical Expert
The World Health Organization says Russian authorities have reported no plague cases in the Irkutsk region.
The worker’s cause of death remains unclear.
A worker at a Siberian research institute that studies plague died after developing pneumonia, prompting officials to monitor and quarantine people who had contact with her and renewing questions about a disease many associate with the Middle Ages.
But Russian authorities have reported no plague cases in the region.
The World Health Organization said Russian officials described the worker’s illness as initially resembling a typical acute respiratory viral infection.
Officials have not publicly established the cause of death.
The worker died Oct. 2 at a hospital near Irkutsk, according to Reuters.
About 200 people who had contact with her were quarantined, and a local official said 60% had since been released.
Russian officials said no plague was found among the contacts who had been tested.
The WHO said it has been in contact with Russian authorities. Reports of the death have fueled speculation online, but Reuters reported there is no public evidence supporting the theories circulating on social media.
The incident has also revived memories of COVID-19.
But plague is not a new or unidentified disease. COVID-19 was caused by a newly identified virus; plague is caused by Yersinia pestis, a well-studied bacterium that persists in animal populations in parts of Africa, Asia and the Americas.
Dr. Leonard Johnson said plague persists in animal populations and continues to cause sporadic human cases around the world, including in the United States.
The CDC has said there is no indication of a broader threat to the United States from the Russian case.
There are three main forms of plague.
Bubonic plague, the most common, typically follows the bite of an infected flea and causes swollen lymph nodes.
Septicemic plague affects the blood; both it and bubonic plague are generally acquired through infected fleas.
Pneumonic plague affects the lungs and can spread through respiratory droplets from an infected person or animal, usually with close contact.
Pneumonic plague can be highly fatal if untreated, said Dr. Leonard Johnson, chief of infectious diseases at Henry Ford St. John Hospital.
But modern antibiotics can treat plague when given promptly. Johnson said people identified as close contacts of a confirmed case could be given preventive antibiotics, including doxycycline or ciprofloxacin, to reduce the chance of secondary infections.
He said the risk of wider spread remains low, particularly in the United States. That is a sharp contrast with the medieval epidemics that killed millions.
Experts remain cautious because they do not have direct access to the underlying information, and public statements by Russian authorities have not clearly established the cause of death.
So far, however, reports do not confirm plague or indicate a wider outbreak.

articles.title_orig: Democrats sue US President Trump over taxpayer-funded ad campaign
articles.title_zh: Democrats sue US President Trump over taxpayer-funded ad campaign
articles.content_orig:
The Democratic National Committee has filed a lawsuit against United States President Donald Trump over television advertisements that were publicly funded and allegedly used to promote his political policies.
Ken Martin, who heads the Democratic Party’s leadership body, suggested in a statement on Wednesday that the ads were designed to bolster Republican odds in the upcoming November 3 midterm elections .
“Donald Trump is misusing millions of taxpayer dollars to fund pure propaganda ads in a last-ditch attempt to save Republicans in November,” Martin said.
Later that day, Common Cause, a democracy watchdog group, filed a second lawsuit over the same set of ads.
It argued that the ads were “overtly political” and therefore ran afoul of laws that bar public funds from being used for political propaganda.
“These ads are not public-service announcements,” Common Cause said in its lawsuit, citing a justification Trump has offered for the television spots. “They are personal publicity and political propaganda through and through.”
Both lawsuits argue that, to create the ad campaign, Trump directed the White House to repurpose $20m in funds that Congress allocated for commemorative activities related to border security, including for those killed in the line of duty.
That manoeuvre, they argue, violates the separation of powers established in the US Constitution.
“The founders made clear more than 200 years ago that the executive can spend money only according to Congress’s direction,” Common Cause’s lawsuit said.
The two lawsuits also point to a provision Congress includes in its appropriations bills barring the use of taxpayer funds for “publicity or propaganda purposes”.
Both complaints seek to have the ads declared illegal, and the expenditures stopped. They also call for steps to be taken to recover any money already spent on the ads.
The Democrats’ lawsuit was filed in Washington, DC, while the Common Cause complaint will be heard in the Southern District of New York.
Trump has faced mounting criticism over the ads, which began airing in September.
So far, the advertising campaign has cost more than $12m to run, according to the media tracking firm AdImpact.
The $20m Trump tapped for the ads comes from a $175m package Congress assigned to the Department of Homeland Security as part of Trump’s immigration enforcement agenda.
Critics have pointed out that one of the ads appears nearly identical to a television spot Trump used in his 2024 re-election campaign.
Three ads have aired so far. In one, a choir sings “love me” over a montage of Trump as he declares the US will “never be a communist country”. Another uses images of Mount Rushmore as Trump heralds a new “golden age of America”.
The third is darker: Trump walks towards the camera in black and white, warning of a “final battle” against the “deep state” and other perceived enemies.
On Wednesday, the news agency Reuters and the research firm Ipsos released a poll showing the ads are highly unpopular . Some 86 percent of the Americans surveyed, including four out of five Republicans, said it was inappropriate for Trump to have used public money for them.
Trump has defended the ads as “promotion for the country”, and he has argued they were similar to public outreach campaigns put out by previous administrations.
But after a bipartisan backlash, Trump said on Monday that taxpayer funds would no longer be used for future ads .
He did not, however, commit to paying back the money already spent on the existing ads.
Members of Trump’s Republican Party have been among those speaking out against the ad campaign.
Senator Thom Tillis, a Republican from North Carolina, said the advertisements resembled something former Hungarian leader Viktor Orban would put out.
Senate Majority Leader John Thune, meanwhile, indicated he agreed with the message in one of the advertisements, but he emphasised that “it shouldn’t be paid for with taxpayer dollars”.

articles.title_orig: Margaret Hamilton, trailblazer whose software powered Apollo 11 moon landing, dies at 90
articles.title_zh: Margaret Hamilton, trailblazer whose software powered Apollo 11 moon landing, dies at 90
articles.content_orig:
MIT computer scientist led development of software for moon mission and earned Presidential Medal of Freedom
Margaret Hamilton, the computer pioneer whose software powered the first moon landing, has died, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) announced on Wednesday. She was 90.
In an era before titles such as software engineer and computer scientist became mainstream, Hamilton, who died on 30 September, learned to program under the tutelage of a renowned MIT meteorologist.
She continued to perfect the craft in an MIT laboratory, writing software that could detect enemy aircraft. When the institute received a Nasa contract to develop the Apollo onboard flight software, she jumped at the opportunity.
“I was attracted both by the sheer idea and the fact that it had never been done before. I was the first programmer to join and the first woman they hired,” she told the Guardian in 2019.
In 1969, minutes before the Apollo 11 spacecraft was set to make history by landing on the lunar surface, an onboard computer’s alarm rang, indicating an emergency.
Faced with a decision of whether to abort the mission, the spacecraft continued on. The software was working just as Hamilton and her team intended.
“It quickly became clear the software was not only informing everyone that there was a hardware-related problem but was compensating for it – restarting and re-establishing the highest priority tasks. The error detection and recovery mechanisms had come to the rescue,” Hamilton said.
Barack Obama referenced the incident when he presented her with the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 2016.
“Our astronauts didn’t have much time, but thankfully they had Margaret Hamilton,” he said.
Hamilton is survived by her daughter, a son-in-law, two grandsons and four great grandchildren, according to MIT.
Reflecting on the mission, in a 2009 interview with MIT News, Hamilton said: “Looking back, we were the luckiest people in the world; there was no choice but to be pioneers; no time to be beginners.”

articles.title_orig: California woman accused of spying for China will be jailed while awaiting trial
articles.title_zh: California woman accused of spying for China will be jailed while awaiting trial
articles.content_orig:
LOS ANGELES — A California woman accused of acting as a Chinese spy inside the U.S. will remain jailed pending her trial after a judge sided Wednesday with federal prosecutors who argued that she poses a flight risk.
Wanying Zhang, 34, who sometimes goes by Heather, will remain in pretrial detention following the ruling by U.S. Magistrate Judge Steve Kim. The FBI arrested her Sunday at Los Angeles International Airport before she could board a flight to China.
In a criminal complaint, prosecutors accused Zhang of spying on a son of Taiwan’s president outside his residence in the Seattle area at the behest of Chinese officials. Zhang, of Irvine, about 42 miles southeast of downtown Los Angeles, hadn’t registered as a foreign agent as required, they said.
Zhang was represented in court Wednesday by veteran criminal defense attorney Craig Harbaugh, who argued she wouldn’t flee in part because of her strong family connections to Southern California, where she lives with her husband and two young daughters.
“The government’s theory — she’s been a sleeper agent for the last 10 years, working as a real estate agent, raising her family and will choose to go to China and abandon her work, her family and her home — it’s not supported,” Harbaugh said.
Zhang’s family had been willing to put up their home equity — valued at $700,000 — combined with bonds from her husband, his sister, his father and a family friend totaling $120,000 as an assurance that she would appear in court.
But prosecutors countered that she had “hundreds of thousands of dollars available to her” in China, as well as investments in a business and contacts that could allow her to flee easily.
“I don’t think it’s a very strong argument that she’s that tied to her family here,” Assistant U.S. Attorney Amanda Elbogen said, casting Zhang as a lying foreign agent with the skills and resources to evade detection and capture.
An investigation found Zhang attended China’s University of International Relations, which an FBI investigator said in court documents is “closely affiliated with China’s intelligence apparatus.”
The charging document alleges Zhang had been communicating with a former classmate, who is now believed to be a Chinese official, through whom she had arranged an agreement to conduct surveillance of the Taiwanese president’s son. The document says she later captured photos, video and license plate information about him and sent them to her alleged Chinese handler.
She is alleged to have done all of that alongside an unidentified “Individual 1,” according to the complaint, who prosecutors said Wednesday had already fled to China two weeks ago.
Zhang wore a white jail jumpsuit and remained shackled for the entirety of Wednesday’s proceedings, a departure from her initial appearance Monday, when she was uncuffed and wore street clothes, with her hair neatly styled.
Wednesday’s hearing had several testy moments among prosecutors, Harbaugh and Kim, largely over whether Zhang’s pattern of one-way flights overseas was a credible defense that she wasn’t a flight risk and whether she had other U.S. properties to rely on for monetary assets.
Discussion in court revealed Zhang had disclosed only one residence to pretrial services, while her husband later revealed they owned two more, which her attorney said was a misunderstanding.
“She lied to pretrial services. She’s a real estate agent; she should know what properties she owns,” Elbogen countered.
Zhang is due back in court as early as Oct. 19 for a preliminary hearing — if federal prosecutors don’t indict her before then.
David Douglas is a supervising producer for NBC News based in Los Angeles.

articles.title_orig: CNBC Daily Open: Another Fed hike is on the horizon — but when?
articles.title_zh: CNBC Daily Open: Another Fed hike is on the horizon — but when?
articles.content_orig:
Hello, this is Justina Lee writing to you from Singapore. Welcome to another edition of CNBC's Daily Open.
Meeting minutes released Wednesday showed that U.S. Fed officials expect interest rates to increase before year-end, but the meeting summary provided no indication of when specifically it would happen.
The U.S. Treasury selling $39 billion of 10-year notes in an auction knocked yields off their highs, while the S&P also pulled back from its record high on Wednesday.
South Korean tech giant Samsung posted a third-quarter preliminary operating profit that exceeded 100 trillion won for the first time in its history, while Lululemon poached Athleta CEO Maggie Gauger.
Traders are bracing themselves for another hike from the U.S. Federal Reserve this year, after meeting minutes released Wednesday showed that Fed officials expect to increase interest rates before the end of the year in order to fend off inflation that has run above target for more than five years.
However, the meeting summary did not show when the hike would occur – only that a stable labor market and persistently higher prices would likely lead to a second hike this year. Rates will be decided by the Fed on Oct. 28 and then again on Dec. 9.
Meanwhile, U.S. Treasury yields backed off their highs after the Treasury sold $39 billion of 10-year notes in an auction. According to BMO, the sale was "strong," with higher than average bidding from non-dealers.
The benchmark 10-year Treasury note yield reached its highest level since April 2002 at 5.365% on Wednesday. The 30-year bond yield also hit its highest level since May 2002 at 5.732%.
Meanwhile, the S&P also pulled back from its record high on Wednesday. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 0.66%, while the S&P 500 slipped 0.22%. The Nasdaq Composite was 0.22% lower.
In Asia, Japan's Nikkei 225 closed 0.92% lower. South Korea's Kospi declined nearly 2% and Australia's benchmark S&P/ASX 200 ended flat. Mainland China market remained closed for the Golden Week holiday on Wednesday.
Meanwhile, the spotlight is back on South Korea's tech sector, after Samsung Electronics posted a third-quarter preliminary operating profit of 107.40 trillion won ($80.2 billion). This is the first time in its history that the company has exceeded 100 trillion won, propelled by booming AI demand. Samsung is expected to release its full third-quarter earnings, including a breakdown by business division, later this month.
In the consumer sector, Lululemon said Wednesday that Athleta CEO Maggie Gauger is joining the company as president and chief product officer , with effect from later this month. The news comes as the athleisure space becomes increasingly competitive.
Over in the oil markets, concerns over supply disruptions slightly eased, after member states of the International Energy Agency agreed to help address rising fuel prices by prioritizing the release of diesel stocks .
Trump doesn’t think Russia plague incident is bioweapon, plans Putin call Wednesday
President Donald Trump said Wednesday that the U.S. does not think the death of a Russian laboratory worker from a suspected case of plague is the result of a bioweapon.
Trump also said he planned to call Russian President Vladimir Putin , who turned 74 on Wednesday, later in the day. Trump previously had said that call would focus on the plague-related incident.
Trump's comments came at an Oval Office event promoting Trump Accounts , the new tax-deferred savings and investment accounts that more than 60 million American children under age 18 have been automatically enrolled in.
